items.title: Les Brésiliens se rendent aux urnes dans un contexte de forte polarisation
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle
items.summary: Les Brésiliens se rendront aux urnes dimanche pour le premier tour d'une élection annoncée très serrée, après une campagne marquée par des scandales de corruption, des inquiétudes économiques et des accusations d'ingérence américaine.
items.body:
Les Brésiliens se rendront aux urnes dimanche pour le premier tour d'une élection annoncée très serrée, après une campagne marquée par des scandales de corruption, des inquiétudes économiques et des accusations d'ingérence américaine.
Le président de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, âgé de 80 ans, brigue un quatrième mandat, tandis que le sénateur Flávio Bolsonaro, âgé de 45 ans, fils de l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro, espère ramener au pouvoir le mouvement d'extrême droite de son père.
Une victoire du sénateur prolongerait la vague de succès remportés en Amérique latine par des candidats proches du président américain Donald Trump, tandis qu'une réélection de Lula pourrait constituer un nouveau défi pour Washington, qui s'est heurté à Lula sur les questions commerciales et de sécurité.
Malgré les inquiétudes croissantes concernant les finances publiques du Brésil et la faiblesse de la croissance économique, la campagne a donné lieu à peu de débats politiques, les deux principaux candidats ayant boudé les grands débats télévisés.
Si aucun candidat n'obtient plus de 50% des suffrages valides, les deux personnes arrivées en tête s'affronteront le 25 octobre. Les sondages indiquent que Lula et Flávio Bolsonaro sont à peu près à égalité dans un éventuel second tour.
Les autres candidats, notamment les anciens gouverneurs d'État Ronaldo Caiado et Romeu Zema, ont peiné à percer face à un électorat polarisé, alors même que Lula et Flávio Bolsonaro sont chacun rejetés par environ la moitié des électeurs, selon les enquêtes d'opinion.
Flávio Bolsonaro a promis de demander l'amnistie pour son père, qui purge une peine de prison de plus de 27 ans pour avoir fomenté un coup d'État après sa défaite électorale en 2022. Lula a présenté cette élection comme un choix entre "la démocratie et le négationnisme" et a mis en garde à plusieurs reprises contre toute ingérence étrangère.
L'OMBRE DE DONALD TRUMP Les répercussions de la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro l'année dernière ont largement marqué la campagne.
Donald Trump, qui avait qualifié cette affaire de "chasse aux sorcières", a imposé en 2025 des droits de douane de 50% au Brésil, liant explicitement ces mesures au procès de Jair Bolsonaro, après que la famille de l'ancien président brésilien a exercé des pressions sur la Cour suprême brésilienne pour qu'elle abandonne les poursuites.
Donald Trump a imposé cette année de nouveaux droits de douane sur les produits en provenance du Brésil au motif de pratiques commerciales jugées déloyales. Lula a vu dans cette décision une tentative d'influencer l'élection et a dépeint les Bolsonaro comme trop désireux de plaire à Washington aux dépens du Brésil.
Les alliés de Lula ont averti que l'administration de Donald Trump pourrait refuser de reconnaître les résultats de l'élection s'il remportait le scrutin. Ils évoquent une tentative avortée d'envoyer des responsables américains au Brésil afin de "discuter de l'intégrité électorale", selon le Département d'État américain.
Reuters a rapporté mercredi que des responsables des services de renseignement brésiliens avaient informé une délégation française et allemande de l'ingérence présumée des Etats-Unis et de la Russie avant l'élection. Les Etats-Unis ont rejeté ces allégations d'ingérence.
Donald Trump n'a pas officiellement apporté son soutien à un candidat, même s'il a reçu le sénateur Flávio Bolsonaro à la Maison blanche et l'ait félicité publiquement.
Le sénateur, qui s'est engagé à resserrer les liens avec les Etats-Unis et Israël, a salué la décision de l'administration Trump de qualifier les principaux gangs brésiliens de "groupes terroristes", une mesure que Lula avait rejetée.
L'accès des Etats-Unis aux vastes réserves brésiliennes de minerais stratégiques est également un enjeu crucial dans le cadre des initiatives de Washington visant à réduire sa dépendance vis-à-vis de la Chine pour ces matières premières.
DIFFICULTÉS ÉCONOMIQUES Malgré la baisse des inégalités et du chômage, Lula a eu du mal à convaincre les électeurs confrontés au coût élevé de la vie, à l'endettement important des ménages et à la menace de la criminalité de rue et d'une activité des gangs de plus en plus répandue.
Flávio Bolsonaro a cherché à tirer parti des préoccupations liées au coût de la vie, tandis que Lula a pris des mesures pour interdire les jeux d'argent en ligne, tout en renforçant les aides sociales et en proposant un nouvel allègement de l'endettement des ménages.
Alors que les dépenses augmentent et que la dette publique a dépassé 82% du PIB, le président brésilien pourrait devoir faire face à des inquiétudes budgétaires. Le gouvernement a revu à la baisse ses prévisions de croissance économique pour cette année et l'an prochain, les ramenant respectivement à seulement 2,0% et 2,3%.
" Lula devrait maintenir un modèle dirigé par l'État avec une modération budgétaire modeste; Bolsonaro devrait quant à lui mener un programme plus favorable au marché, axé sur les réductions de dépenses, les privatisations, les concessions et un ancrage budgétaire plus solide", a déclaré Alberto Ramos, chef économiste pour l'Amérique latine chez Goldman Sachs.
Les électeurs éliront également dimanche les 513 membres de la Chambre des représentants et les deux tiers du Sénat.
Depuis la destitution de l'ancienne présidente Dilma Rousseff, alliée de Lula, en 2016, le Congrès a acquis une influence accrue sur la politique brésilienne, ce qui a renforcé les enjeux des élections législatives.

items.title: Yemeni government launches offensive to seize all areas from Iran-backed Houthis
items.author: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: Despite the preparations for a counteroffensive, the Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive that saw government forces collapse.
items.body:
Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday it was launching a major military campaign to recapture all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis .
The government’s armed forces would press the offensive “until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia,” Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address. A military spokesman later called on the Houthis to lay down their weapons.
The Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, have held Yemen’s capital Sanaa and vast parts of the northwest, where most of the population live, since 2014. They have so far withstood a series of attacks over the years by Saudi Arabia, the UAE and their Western allies, and have updated their weaponry with the help of Iran.
The movement launched a surprise offensive last month which captured the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait and some 150 km (90 miles) of coast on the Red Sea in a matter of weeks, giving the Houthis new leverage over the international shipping route.
That advance also opened a new front in the wider US-Israeli war launched in February against Iran, to which Tehran’s responses included choking oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz , to the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.
HOUTHIS SAY THEY STRUCK SAUDI ARABIA As the Yemeni government, known as the Presidential Leadership Council, made its announcement, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia.
They claimed the attacks caused major fires and were in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all chances of de-escalating the conflict had been exhausted.
He thanked Saudi Arabia for its support and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support PLC forces and institutions.
Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to [USN:L8N45M1W0 TEXT:"launch an assault"] on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground.
NEW FRONT IN MIDEAST WAR The US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters.
The United States’ war on Iran has decimated a layer of Iranian military and political leadership, but has also entangled Washington in a new engagement in the Middle East and depleted crucial military hardware.
Yemen has been mired in conflict for years, with an array of local armed groups and factions backed by competing regional and international actors.
After a popular uprising that was part of the Arab Spring movements in 2011, the Houthis, an armed group of Zaidi Shi’ite Muslims, captured Sanaa.
The Saudi-backed PLC, which is also recognised by the United Nations, has since the Houthi takeover controlled the south and east of the country, based in the former South Yemen capital of Aden.
Saudi Arabia entered Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the PLC, but failed to defeat the Houthis.
A truce agreed between the warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
HOUTHIS ON FRONT FOOT The Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground since seizing control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in their lightning offensive last month that saw government forces collapse.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.
In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast.
Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed.
The city is important not just for its strategic location; Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country.
Three in four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

items.title: Hamilton says 'heart sank' as tyre gamble backfired before stunning Sepang recovery
items.author: Rohith Nair
items.creator: Rohith Nair
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton said he had mixed emotions after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia where he started second on the grid but dropped to 18th when a tyre gamble went wrong before fighting to finish third in a chaotic, rain-hit race on Sunday.
items.body:
Lewis Hamilton said he had mixed emotions after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia where he started second on the grid but dropped to 18th when a tyre gamble went wrong before fighting to finish third in a [USN:L1N45Q023 TEXT:"chaotic, rain-hit race"] on Sunday.
After [USN:L1N45Q01D TEXT:"rain delayed the start of the race"] by more than 90 minutes, Hamilton was one of the few drivers who switched from intermediate tyres to slicks on a track that was still drying.
The Briton had a slow start and then found himself going backwards, falling as low as 18th, but he opted to stick with his strategy despite Ferrari calling him back into the pits for a tyre change.
Hamilton then carved his way through the field as the track dried up while safety cars also came to his rescue, with the veteran eventually overtaking Red Bull's Isack Hadjar in the dying stages to secure a podium behind Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli.
"As a team, we ended up taking that soft (tyre) and at the end of the pit lane, these two (Verstappen and Antonelli) took off their (tyre) blankets and my heart just sank, because I knew straight away that we were in trouble," Hamilton told reporters.
"As we pulled out, all the spray came out the back of Max's car and I was like, 'Okay, I'm done. My race is really in trouble'.
"We made the decision to live with it. As everyone was overtaking me, they (Ferrari) said, 'Should we stop?' I said, 'No, we've already waited another 26 seconds. What's the difference'."
But as the track dried and safety car deployments played into his hands, Hamilton began a remarkable recovery drive as he gave Hadjar chase for fourth place, before [USN:L4N45Q017 TEXT:"George Russell's retirement"] gave him a shot at a podium.
"I just waited for the track to dry and once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great. Then after that, really good pit stops from my guys in the garage," Hamilton added.
"And then a good strategy. So for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that's what was going to be the case. I'm really, really grateful."
His teammate Charles Leclerc also salvaged fourth place for Ferrari and he conceded that was the best they could have achieved considering how much faster Red Bull and Mercedes were.
"Honestly, the first part of the race, everything that could have gone wrong went wrong. And on the second part, everything that could have gone right went our way," Leclerc said.
"So at the end of the day, I prefer it that way than the other way around. We were P4 today and I honestly think that with a normal race we would have finished P3 and P4. The two guys in front were just way too quick for us.
"Lewis had quite a good pace. I struggled a lot with the car, which we're looking into. I had a good feeling on Friday, good feeling until Q2, and then Q3 I started to lose out. Today the race was very tricky."

"As a team, we ended up taking that soft (tyre) and at the end of the pit lane, these two (Verstappen and Antonelli) took off their (tyre) blankets and my heart just sank, because I knew straight away that we were in trouble," Hamilton told reporters.
"As we pulled out, all the spray came out the back of Max's car and I was like, 'Okay, I'm done. My race is really in trouble'.
"We made the decision to live with it. As everyone was overtaking me, they (Ferrari) said, 'Should we stop?' I said, 'No, we've already waited another 26 seconds. What's the difference'."
But as the track dried and safety car deployments played into his hands, Hamilton began a remarkable recovery drive as he gave Hadjar chase for fourth place, before George Russell's retirement gave him a shot at a podium.
"I just waited for the track to dry and once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great. Then after that, really good pit stops from my guys in the garage," Hamilton added.
"And then a good strategy. So for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that's what was going to be the case. I'm really, really grateful."
His teammate Charles Leclerc also salvaged fourth place for Ferrari and he conceded that was the best they could have achieved considering how much faster Red Bull and Mercedes were.
"Honestly, the first part of the race, everything that could have gone wrong went wrong. And on the second part, everything that could have gone right went our way," Leclerc said.
"So at the end of the day, I prefer it that way than the other way around. We were P4 today and I honestly think that with a normal race we would have finished P3 and P4. The two guys in front were just way too quick for us.
"Lewis had quite a good pace. I struggled a lot with the car, which we're looking into. I had a good feeling on Friday, good feeling until Q2, and then Q3 I started to lose out. Today the race was very tricky."

items.title: Saudi Arabia to cancel Joy Awards, its answer to the Grammys, amid budget cuts, sources say
items.author: Timour Azhari
items.creator: Timour Azhari
items.summary: Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year's Joy Awards, its star-studded answer to the Oscars or the Grammys, as financial strain and the Iran war hit the country's nascent entertainment sector, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year's Joy Awards, its star-studded answer to the Oscars or the Grammys, as financial strain and the Iran war hit the country's nascent entertainment sector, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
Held in January, the event has become the crown jewel of Riyadh's annual events calendar, drawing performers including Katy Perry and Robbie Williams this year and handing out awards in music as well as other areas of entertainment and sport.
It is the latest high-profile entertainment event to face cancellation or postponement as Riyadh reprioritizes spending and cuts culture and entertainment budgets.
A spokesperson for the General Entertainment Authority, which organizes the Joy Awards along with Saudi media conglomerate MBC Group, did not respond to a request for comment. MBC Group and the Saudi government's media office also did not respond to requests for comment.
Industry sources say budget cuts were already felt before the Iran war, which has undermined Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's efforts to turn the kingdom into a destination for tourism and global events under his ambitious Vision 2030 plan.
Flagship projects scaled back or indefinitely postponed over the last year or so include the 100-mile (161 km) steel and glass tower The Line at megacity NEOM, and a $50 billion steel and metal [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"cube"] in Riyadh. The government has also withdrawn funding from ventures such as LIV Golf, after spending over $5 billion on the startup, and is now quietly shelving plans to [USN:L6N45E0H2 TEXT:"build"] the NEOM Stadium, one of the main projects for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said.
"The war and its wider ripple effects are inevitably prompting Gulf states to reassess spending priorities," said Mazen Hayek, a Dubai-based media consultant.
"It's not simply a question of whether governments have the financial capacity to fund such initiatives. Some of these events were also conceived as instruments of international visibility, soft power and influence. In the current environment, however, governments may be weighing those objectives against other national priorities," he said.
FILM FESTIVAL, DESERT RAVE ALSO CANCELLED Last month, the Red Sea Film Festival was postponed until 2027, with organizers citing logistical constraints and other factors. Uncertainty over the Iran war has also made it difficult to book international stars for such events, the industry sources said.
The Red Sea Film Festival was launched in 2021 as part of an effort to develop local cinema after Saudi Arabia lifted a decades-long ban on cinemas.
Last month, organizers also called off Soundstorm, a city-sized rave in the desert due to be held in December that welcomes hundreds of thousands of partygoers and was headlined by Cardi B last year. Organizers said it would return next year, giving no reason for the cancellation.
Soundstorm, also known as MDLBEAST, began in 2019 as new events were staged amid rapid social change under the crown prince, widely known as MbS, whose reforms sought to rein in the power of religious conservatives.
With gender-mixing, dancing and displays of queer culture, the festival often drew the ire of religious conservatives and stunned even some of those who support other aspects of the kingdom's social opening.
Events aimed at driving investment into the kingdom, such as the flagship Future Investment Initiative (FII) taking place at the end of this month, remain scheduled as planned, according to organizers.
"Events that are important for the Saudi economy and showing its place in the world are still being prioritised; what isn't is anything that is singing and dancing and having a good time," a person working in the Saudi events industry said.

items.title: Can America Break China’s Grip on Rare Earths?
items.summary: China spent decades building a dominant position across rare-earth mining, processing and magnet manufacturing, leaving the US dependent on a foreign supply chain for materials essential to everything from vehicles and wind turbines to electronics and defense systems. MP Materials is now trying to rebuild that chain domestically, moving from its Mountain Pass mine in California into refining. But catching up will take more than finding minerals: the US still faces higher costs, limited processing capacity, opaque pricing and a Chinese lead that industry experts say took roughly 25 years to build. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vota no Rio e reitera expectativa de vitória em 1ºturno
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O candidato à Presidência pelo PL, Flávio Bolsonaro, votou na manhã deste domingo em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, pouco após a abertura das urnas. Ele entrou em sua seção acompanhado da esposa Fernanda.
items.body:
O candidato à Presidência pelo PL, Flávio Bolsonaro, votou na manhã deste domingo em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, pouco após a abertura das urnas. Ele entrou em sua seção acompanhado da esposa Fernanda.
Em breve fala a jornalistas após a votação, o senador voltou a afirmar que espera vencer já no primeiro turno, citando pesquisas internas da sua campanha.
"As nossas pesquisas internas mostram que a gente ultrapassou no primeiro turno já faz algum tempo", disse Flávio Bolsonaro. "Espero que seja suficiente para dar vitória no primeiro turno."
"Estou mais que preparado para presidir este país e devolver às pessoas o direito de sonhar", acrescentou.
Pesquisas divulgadas no sábado, no entanto, [USN:L6N45O13P TEXT:"mostraram"] um cenário de empate técnico de Flávio com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição, com grande probabilidade de a disputa seguir para o segundo turno.
Políticos do PL também acompanharam Flávio até a seção, incluindo o candidato ao governo do Estado Douglas Ruas (PL). Flávio ainda acompanharia a votação da esposa, no bairro da Tijuca, e em seguida a previsão é que retorne a Brasília, de onde acompanhará a apuração dos votos.

items.title: Kraken eager to douse Flames again in home opener
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Seattle Kraken nearly got all they could have wanted on their season-opening trip to Alberta.
items.body:
The Seattle Kraken nearly got all they could have wanted on their season-opening trip to Alberta.
After a 6-1 victory Thursday in Calgary, the Kraken took host Edmonton down to the final minutes before former Hart Trophy winners Leon Draisaitl and Connor McDavid scored in the final 2:27 in the Oilers' 3-1 win on Saturday. Kraken goaltender Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 24 shots in the loss.
The Kraken have their home opener scheduled for Sunday in a rematch against Calgary, which lost 4-1 Saturday night in Vancouver.
"We got a great, solid effort from 'Grubie,'" Kraken coach Lane Lambert said after the Edmonton game. "It's unfortunate that we don't come out of here with more than what we have, but we have to find ways to come out of buildings like this when the score is tied late.
"That's a step for us that we have to get to, for sure, but I thought there were a lot of good things in the game (Saturday)."
The Kraken, who finished 31st among 32 NHL teams on penalty kills last season, stopping just 72.2% of their short-handed situations, held Edmonton scoreless in three attempts. The Oilers led the NHL by converting 30.6% of their man-advantage attempts in 2025-26 and were a combined 3-for-9 in their first two games of this campaign.
Draisaitl's go-ahead goal came after Oilers defenseman Ryan Shea banked the puck off the boards to keep it in the offensive zone. The puck caromed off McDavid's knee to Draisaitl near the top right of the crease, and Draisaitl quickly put a shot past Grubauer.
McDavid capped the scoring with an empty-net goal.
"I think we deserved a better result," said Kraken forward Bobby McMann, who scored on the power play midway through the second period. "When you see ones like that (Draisaitl goal), you sometimes realize that's the game of hockey and you want to put yourself in a position where something like that maybe doesn't matter as much because we have a goal up.
"There's always ways to counteract that, but yeah, those ones are always tough to see when a game's so close and you're playing so well down the stretch toward the end of a game."
The Kraken trounced the Flames in the season opener as defenseman Vince Dunn collected a goal and two assists, Jared McCann added three assists and Matty Beniers and Kaapo Kakko each had a goal and an assist. Joey Daccord made 24 saves, losing the shutout bid with 3:25 remaining.
The Flames took a 1-0 lead into the third period Saturday in Vancouver before surrendering four unanswered goals.
Matt Coronato scored and Devin Cooley made 22 saves for Calgary.
"We were a much different team tonight than we were our first game of the year, so there's a lot of things that we can build off of from this game," Flames coach Ryan Huska said. "Couple things again we got to clean up, but there's a lot we can build off."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Australia probes flydubai co-pilot's links to the country, police say
items.author: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
items.creator: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
items.summary: The co-pilot, identified as an Omani, studied at a university in Melbourne, sources said.
items.body:
A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is investigating links to Australia of the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, who stabbed his captain and then [USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"attempted to hijack"] the plane, a police spokesperson said on Sunday.
The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team – which comprises federal police, Victorian state police and the ASIO intelligence agency – was "investigating the man's links to Australia," the Australian Federal Police spokesperson said.
Two sources briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne, the capital of the Australian state of Victoria. A third source said he studied at RMIT University around a decade ago. RMIT declined to comment.
The co-pilot of the [USN:L1N45P02M TEXT:"flydubai flight FZ1073"], which was bound for Israel from Dubai on Wednesday, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:S8N43T02Z TEXT:"terrorist attack"]".
Flight FZ1073 would have felt like a [USN:L4N45Q00M TEXT:""vertical roller coaster""], when it plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.
CO-PILOT IN CUSTODY IN UAE Two sources have said the co-pilot is an Omani national named Hamam Al-Hamami. Israeli officials have not named the co-pilot but said that he is from Oman. UAE authorities and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilot's identity.
Reuters could not independently reach Al-Hamami, who is in UAE custody, for comment. The UAE has not announced any formal charges against him and it is not known if he has appointed legal counsel. Oman has not commented on the incident.
Disaster on board flight FZ1073 was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew. The UAE public prosecutor has said the co-pilot had attempted to take control of the plane.
RADICAL MOSQUES AND EXTREMIST WEBSITES Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals.
A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities and later transferred to the UAE on Thursday.
The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Al-Hamami had allegedly visited what it described as radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation. Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to the Financial Times.
Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. The government of Australia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal business hours.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone radical [USN:L6N45N0GW TEXT:"Islamist indoctrination"] and was clearly suicidal, although he has not said when or where that indoctrination allegedly occurred.
On Sunday he instructed the National Security Council to appoint an examiner to "conduct a thorough review of all security aspects regarding foreign civil aviation to Israel".
Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has also said pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It is not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv.

items.title: Irã diz que Estreito de Ormuz não será reaberto até que condições sejam atendidas
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O Estreito de Ormuz não será reaberto até que sejam cumpridas as sete condições iranianas estabelecidas em um acordo provisório firmado em junho com os EUA, segundo informou a mídia estatal, citando declarações do presidente do Parlamento iraniano, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, no domingo.
items.body:
O Estreito de Ormuz não será reaberto até que sejam cumpridas as sete condições iranianas estabelecidas em um acordo provisório firmado em junho com os EUA, segundo informou a mídia estatal, citando declarações do presidente do Parlamento iraniano, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, no domingo.
O Irã apresentou uma proposta durante a Assembleia Geral da ONU segundo a qual a via navegável do Estreito de Ormuz poderia ser reaberta e a passagem marítima normal restabelecida em até sete dias caso as condições fossem cumpridas. Os EUA responderam a essa proposta na semana passada por meio de intermediários do Catar.
“A posição da República Islâmica do Irã é totalmente clara e firme, e o Estreito de Ormuz não será reaberto até que nossas sete condições, baseadas no Memorando de Entendimento de Islamabad, sejam cumpridas”, disse Qalibaf, principal negociador do Irã, segundo a reportagem.
Ele afirmou que Washington “precisa compreender que o período de prolongamento do processo (diplomático) e de imposição de exigências unilaterais chegou ao fim”.
Um porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores afirmou no domingo que Teerã havia esclarecido suas posições gerais, por meio de mediadores, em resposta aos EUA, mas que ainda havia pontos adicionais a serem comunicados a Washington.
“As propostas dos norte-americanos estão mais ou menos alinhadas com suas posições anteriores, especificamente sobre a questão nuclear. Dissemos a eles que nosso foco nesta fase é a questão do Estreito de Ormuz e que o retorno à segurança nessa via navegável exige medidas claras por parte dos EUA”, declarou o porta-voz Esmaeil Baghaei.
Ele também negou que Teerã tivesse oferecido à agência nuclear da ONU inspeções em suas instalações nucleares em troca do alívio das sanções dos EUA, afirmando que o Irã não havia iniciado negociações nucleares com Washington.
O documento que está circulando delineia um período de sete dias para a construção de confiança, com o objetivo de levar as duas partes de volta a uma versão aprimorada do memorando de entendimento acordado em junho, incluindo medidas concretas sobre o programa nuclear do Irã, disse na semana passada uma autoridade a par das negociações.
A divergência gira em torno da sequência das medidas, e não dos componentes do plano, acrescentou a autoridade.
O Catar vem transmitindo mensagens entre Washington e Teerã em um esforço para pôr fim ao conflito e reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz, por onde passava um quinto do petróleo e do gás natural liquefeito do mundo antes da guerra que começou no final de fevereiro com ataques dos EUA e de Israel ao Irã.

items.title: Protests intensify in India over demands for election chief to quit
items.author: Saurabh Sharma
items.creator: Saurabh Sharma
items.summary: Thousands of youth protesters and opposition supporters rallied in Delhi and Mumbai on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election commission chief over changes to voter rolls, as police detained some demonstrators for a third day.
items.body:
Thousands of youth protesters and opposition supporters rallied in Delhi and Mumbai on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election commission chief over changes to voter rolls, as police detained some demonstrators for a third day.
Opposition leaders Raj Thackeray and Uddhav Thackeray led protests in Mumbai, calling for the revisions to be scrapped and for Election Commission Chief [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] to step down.
The protesters say the changes benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's governing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a charge denied by the Election Commission and the BJP.
In the capital, New Delhi, protesters started gathering in the early evening and some were detained by police, according to a Reuters witness.
Some demonstrators breached police barricades and surrounded vehicles carrying detained demonstrators, climbing onto them and laying on the road to block their path, the witness added.
"Police dragged me by my hair," said Aahna Singh, an activist and political science student at Jawaharlal Nehru University who was protesting. "The police are resorting to brutality."
Delhi Police did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
Police in the capital have prevented protesters from [USN:L4N45P01A TEXT:"assembling"] over the last two days, detaining dozens of them and transporting them away by bus.
Some of the detainees were released later on Friday and Saturday, but police registered cases against some on charges of violating orders banning mass gatherings in the centre of the capital.
PROTESTERS SAY VOTER ROLL CHANGES EXCLUDE MILLIONS The protesters say the nationwide voter-roll revision exercise launched last year has disenfranchised millions of eligible voters by removing them from electoral rolls in a way that will benefit Modi's party.
"I just want to tell the ruling party this much... We are angry about how you are wielding that power. It's the people of this country who should decide who sits in power and who sits in opposition, not the Election Commission," the opposition leader Raj Thackeray said.
The Election Commission says the exercise is designed to remove duplicate, deceased, or ineligible entries and maintain electoral integrity. On Friday, it directed its officials to register eligible voters inadvertently omitted from electoral rolls.
Kumar has not publicly responded to the demands for his resignation or commented on the protests, which look set to continue over the next few days due to more planned rallies.
An alliance of India's opposition parties plans to launch protests to "[USN:L6N45M0NH TEXT:"save democracy"]" with a march to the Election Commission office on Tuesday. The Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party has announced plans for a major rally in Delhi on October 10.
The demonstrations represent the latest in a series of youth-led challenges to Modi's government — unprecedented in his 12 years in power.
In July, student protests forced the ouster of the federal education minister following a leak of question papers for a national medical college entrance examination, marking the worst political crisis of Modi's third term in office.
(This story has been corrected to change the day of the opposition march to Tuesday, not Monday, in the third bullet point and paragraph 14.)

items.title: Russell's championship dreams hit by cruel power unit failure in Sepang
items.author: Rohith Nair
items.creator: Rohith Nair
items.summary: George Russell's Formula One title hopes took a crushing blow when his Mercedes ground to a halt with a power unit failure five laps from the finish, turning what looked like a certain podium into heartbreak at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday.
items.body:
George Russell's Formula One title hopes took a crushing blow when his Mercedes ground to a halt with a power unit failure five laps from the finish, turning what looked like a certain podium into heartbreak at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday.
The British driver was running in a strong position to claim valuable championship points when the second safety car emerged for Alex Albon's Williams, which was stuck in the gravel.
But as the field prepared for a thrilling finale behind the safety car, Russell - who was third behind eventual [USN:L1N45Q023 TEXT:"race winner Max Verstappen"] and Kimi Antonelli - suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he climbed out.
"You've almost got to laugh, it's beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame," Russell said.
"The podium looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race. But not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling."
The retirement meant Russell's championship deficit grew from 66 points to 84 behind Antonelli.
"I don't need to say I think it's (championship hopes) gone or whatever, but of course it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality," Russell added.
"I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side... It's a real shame."
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirmed it was a power unit failure on Russell's car.
"I'm so massively annoyed. I'm not in a happy place," Wolff said.
"First of all we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will."
With the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc finishing third and fourth, Mercedes' lead in the constructors' standings is now 151 points.
"We had such an advantage (with) two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky," Wolff added.
"And to make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.
"So as much as I love to be here, when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest."

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : George Russell's Formula One title hopes took a crushing blow when his Mercedes ground to a halt with a power unit failure five laps from the finish, turning what looked like a certain podium into heartbreak at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday.
The British driver was running in a strong position to claim valuable championship points when the second safety car emerged for Alex Albon's Williams, which was stuck in the gravel.
But as the field prepared for a thrilling finale behind the safety car, Russell - who was third behind eventual race winner Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli - suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he climbed out.
"You've almost got to laugh, it's beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame," Russell said.

"The podium looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race. But not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling."
The retirement meant Russell's championship deficit grew from 66 points to 84 behind Antonelli.
"I don't need to say I think it's (championship hopes) gone or whatever, but of course it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality," Russell added.
"I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side... It's a real shame."
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirmed it was a power unit failure on Russell's car.
"I'm so massively annoyed. I'm not in a happy place," Wolff said.
"First of all we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will."
With the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc finishing third and fourth, Mercedes' lead in the constructors' standings is now 151 points.
"We had such an advantage (with) two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky," Wolff added.
"And to make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.
"So as much as I love to be here, when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest."

items.title: Spanish police clear migrant camp on Ceuta beach ahead of royal visit
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Spanish police on Sunday cleared a migrant camp on a beach in the North African enclave of Ceuta, where tens of thousands crossed the border from Morocco over two months ago, the Spanish government said.
items.body:
Spanish police on Sunday cleared a migrant camp on a beach in the North African enclave of Ceuta, where tens of thousands crossed the border from Morocco over two months ago, the Spanish government said.
More than [USN:L8N43W1SU TEXT:"72,000 crossed the border"] from Morocco into Ceuta in late July. While most of the migrants later went back, at least 10,000 remain in the Spanish enclave in North Africa, straining local resources and fuelling tensions.
Police moved migrants from Trampolin beach, where around 3,000 people were living in tents and makeshift homes for two months, to temporary accommodation where they will be processed or can go back to Morocco, a Spanish interior ministry spokesman told Reuters on Sunday.
Tensions have persisted over the presence of migrants sleeping rough in the tiny enclave, which is home to 80,000 people. Locals held a demonstration on Saturday calling for the migrants to leave.
King Felipe and Queen Letizia are due to visit Ceuta on October 13 to 14 for the first time in his 12-year reign. The visit comes amid longstanding friction with Morocco, which claims sovereignty over both Ceuta and Spain's other North African enclave, Melilla.

items.title: Russia to intensify strikes on Ukraine after Zelenskiy interview
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russia said it would step up attacks on military facilities and defense-industry sites.
items.body:
Russia will intensify strikes on Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine, the Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday, responding to an interview with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in which he vowed increased attacks on Russian refineries.
The ministry said Russian forces would step up attacks on military facilities, defence industry sites and related infrastructure in Kyiv and elsewhere in Ukraine.
Zelenskiy had told Reuters in an interview published on Saturday that [USN:L1N45P05A TEXT:"Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries"] in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to force people to abandon Kyiv and other cities, but will not target civilians.
Russia has recently escalated strikes on infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital, including hitting bridges across the Dnipro river. The intensifying campaign has [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"seriously disrupted life"] for the capital's 3 million residents ahead of the bitter winter months.
The Russian Defence Ministry said its recent strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions were a response to what it described as attacks by Kyiv on civilian targets inside Russia.
Both Russia and Ukraine deny targeting civilians.

items.title: Rugby league-Nawaqanitawase tries fire Roosters to 16th NRL title
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries as the Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the National Rugby League final on Sunday, securing the foundation club a 16th title.
items.body:
Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries as the Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the National Rugby League final on Sunday, securing the foundation club a 16th title.
Nawaqanitawase, who could represent Australia at both the league and union World Cups over the next 12 months, crossed either side of halftime to help crush Newcastle hopes of a massive upset in front of a crowd of 80,814 at Stadium Australia.
Newcastle were looking to take the title back to their industrial port city for the first time since 2001 and scored the first two tries of the contest through Francis Manuleleua and skipper Kalyn Ponga to take an early 12-0 lead.
Nawaqanitawase, playing the final game of his two-year stint at the Roosters before his return to rugby union, cut the deficit from a clever kick and chase five minutes before the break, however.
Newcastle defended several sets on their own line at the start of the second half but Roosters centre Billy Smith forced his way over in the 47th minute for a converted try that locked up the scores at 12-12.
Sam Walker put the Sydney side in front for the first time with a penalty seven minutes later, and Nawaqanitawase added his second try in the right corner before the hour mark to extend the lead to 18-12.
Experienced five-eighth Daly Cherry-Evans, playing his last NRL game before his switch to England's Super League, slotted a field goal to extend the advantage to seven points but the Knights found a second wind in the remaining 11 minutes.
Summoning the spirit of last week's sensational win over the Penrith Panthers with 12 men that got them to the final, they forced their way upfield and winger Greg Marzhew crossed for a converted try that made it a one-point game with four minutes on the clock.
The Roosters, one of the two clubs remaining from the first season of what became the NRL in 1908, held on, however, to secure their first title since 2019 and fourth under long-term coach Trent Robinson.
"Credit to the Knights, they fought for 80 minutes there," said Nawaqanitawase.
"This is going to last me a lifetime, it's sad to go but I love everyone here, I love all the boys, and let's celebrate this win, far out."

items.title: Eleitores vão às urnas com expectativa de resultado apertado entre Lula e Flávio em eleição polarizada
items.author: Eduardo Simões
items.creator: Eduardo Simões
items.summary: Marcada por polêmicas envolvendo desde o Judiciário até a padroeira do Brasil, passando por denúncias generalizadas de corrupção e temores de interferência externa, a campanha eleitoral para a Presidência da República chega ao primeiro turno, neste domingo, com a disputa totalmente em aberto entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), em mais um pleito marcado pela polarização.
items.body:
Marcada por polêmicas envolvendo desde o Judiciário até a padroeira do Brasil, passando por denúncias generalizadas de corrupção e temores de interferência externa, a campanha eleitoral para a Presidência da República chega ao primeiro turno, neste domingo, com a disputa totalmente em aberto entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), em mais um pleito marcado pela polarização.
Os mais de 158,7 milhões de brasileiros aptos a votar começaram a ir às seções eleitorais nesta manhã -- as urnas abriram às 8h e fecham às 17h pelo horário de Brasília -- após meses de embates muitas vezes em nível pessoal de cada lado, em que as propostas para governar o país pelos próximos quatro anos não foram protagonistas.
Lula e Flávio votaram no começo da manhã e manifestaram confiança na vitória.
Ao votar em uma escola em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), Lula fez um apelo para que os eleitores com mais de 70 anos compareçam às urnas e reafirmou que o que está em jogo nas eleições é a escolha entre o "fortalecimento do regime democrático e a barbárie".
Flávio Bolsonaro votou em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, pouco após a abertura das urnas, e disse que espera vencer já no primeiro turno. "As nossas pesquisas internas mostram que a gente ultrapassou no primeiro turno já faz algum tempo", declarou. "Espero que seja suficiente para dar vitória no primeiro turno."
As pesquisas de intenção de voto divulgadas no sábado, no entanto, apontam para uma nova rodada de votação, que aconteceria em 25 de outubro.
Para a eleição acabar neste domingo, é preciso que um dos candidatos conquiste mais de 50% dos votos válidos, quando são desconsiderados os votos brancos e nulos.
Levantamentos do Datafolha e da Quaest colocaram Lula e Flávio em empate técnico no primeiro turno nos votos válidos, com vantagem numérica do atual presidente de 3 pontos na primeira e de 1 ponto na segunda. Uma outra pesquisa, do MDA, colocou Lula com 47,8% dos votos válidos contra 42,1% de Flávio.
O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou confiar em um processo tranquilo de votação: "Amanhecemos o dia hoje com a segurança de que as eleições vão transcorrer na maior normalidade", disse, ao votar em Brasília.
A campanha chegou ao fim sem que Lula e Flávio tenham se enfrentado diretamente. No debate da TV Bandeirantes, ambos decidiram não ir, deixando os púlpitos vazios com seus nomes para serem criticados por Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão) e Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), que estavam presentes. Romeu Zema (Novo) completa a lista dos outros candidatos cujos partidos têm representação no Congresso, mas cujas intenções de voto jamais se aproximaram da dos dois líderes.
Já o debate da TV Globo, que tradicionalmente encerra as campanhas, acabou sendo [USN:L1N45N18V TEXT:"cancelado"] após uma série de decisões judiciais e da desistência de última hora de Flávio, filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro -- que está atualmente em prisão domiciliar após ser condenado por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Lula havia dito dias antes que não compareceria.
TEMOR DE INTERFERÊNCIA A eleição também ocorre em meio a renovados temores sobre uma possível interferência estrangeira na eleição presidencial brasileira. A Reuters [USN:L6N45M0VR TEXT:"revelou"] na última semana que autoridades francesas e alemãs ouviram de membros da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) que já estariam acontecendo tentativas de interferência dos Estados Unidos e da Rússia no pleito.
Além disso, na quinta-feira, a embaixada dos EUA no Brasil [USN:L6N45O0XD TEXT:"anunciou"] a suspensão dos serviços consulares a partir da última sexta-feira, alegando preocupações não especificadas de segurança. Além disso, a embaixada pediu aos seus funcionários que trabalhassem de casa na sexta após uma ameaça. A embaixadora da Austrália também anunciou o fechamento da representação diplomática do país em Brasília citando o alerta norte-americano.
A medida foi criticada pelo presidente do PT, Edinho Silva, que viu tentativa do governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de influenciar a opinião pública brasileira.
A relação com os EUA e com Trump foi, inclusive, um dos principais marcadores da diferença entre Lula e Flávio. Enquanto o presidente alertou o homólogo norte-americano publicamente a não interferir no Brasil, o senador procurou mostrar proximidade com Trump, inclusive visitando-o na Casa Branca.
"É uma relação tensa porque o Brasil não quer se ver dentro da zona de influência dos EUA. Tradicionalmente a nossa diplomacia é independente. O Lula acredita que, pela boa relação com a China, especialmente a comercial, que manter essa independência é fundamental", disse Leonardo Barreto, cofundador da Think Policy.
"O Flávio tenta fazer dos EUA uma espécie de fiador das eleições. A família Bolsonaro acredita que as eleições não são feitas em condições de liberdade. Desconfiança em relação a urna, meios de comunicação, administração do Judiciário. Buscam no apoio dos americanos uma espécie de pressão para garantir o mínimo de neutralidade das autoridades brasileiras, percebem nos americanos uma espécie de seguro", acrescentou.
BETS, STF E PADROEIRA Em meio a denúncias de corrupção como as do Banco Master e o escândalo do INSS, que atingiram tanto Flávio quanto o filho mais velho de Lula, além de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a campanha também foi marcada pelo apelo do senador ao seu pai, ao mesmo tempo em que buscava se mostrar mais moderado do que o ex-presidente, enquanto Lula seguiu batendo na tecla dos seus três mandatos na Presidência e lançando mão de medidas populares às vésperas do pleito.
Entre elas, o governo anunciou o reajuste de 15% nos benefícios do Bolsa Família, a edição de uma medida provisória para proibir as casas de apostas online, as chamadas bets, e o anúncio da intenção de distribuir gratuitamente pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) as chamadas canetas emagrecedoras, três medidas aprovadas pelo eleitorado, segundo as pesquisas de opinião.
Mas a polêmica que marcou a reta final da campanha ficou por conta de rumores de que Flávio retiraria de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil, o que foi negado com veemência pelo senador. Flávio classificou os boatos de "fake news", enquanto Lula disse que, enquanto for presidente, ninguém irá "avacalhar" com Nossa Senhora.
Além do presidente, os eleitores também escolherão neste domingo os governadores dos 26 Estados e do Distrito Federal, além de 54 dos 81 senadores e dos 513 deputados e dos integrantes das Assembleias Legislativa de 26 Estado e da Câmara Distrital do Distrito Federal.
A eleição para o Senado estará sob o foco, em um momento de pressão sobre ministros do STF, que podem sofrer impeachment pelos integrantes da Casa, e em um momento em que estão [USN:L6N45N0ZL TEXT:"vagas"] funções em órgãos reguladores, como o Banco Central, cujos nomes precisam ser aprovados pelo Senado.

items.title: Verstappen wins chaotic rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
items.author: Rohith Nair
items.creator: Rohith Nair
items.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday for his first victory of the season after the race start was delayed by more than 90 minutes due to treacherous conditions at the Sepang International Circuit.
items.body:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday for his first victory of the season after the race start was [USN:L1N45Q01D TEXT:"delayed by more than 90 minutes"] due to treacherous conditions at the Sepang International Circuit.
Verstappen was the last driver to win in Sepang in 2017 before it was taken off the calendar and the Dutchman, who had also taken pole, gave Red Bull a first victory with their own power unit despite an early setback when he lost the lead before turn one.
"It's a really nice one after the year that we've had and the progression that we've made. So I'm incredibly proud of everyone. It is super nice to win here," said Verstappen.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second for Mercedes and now has an 84-point lead over his closest rival and teammate George Russell, who was third when he retired with a suspected power unit issue with five laps remaining.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished third despite a tyre gamble that had dropped the Briton down to 18th at the start of the race.
"Obviously, we had the wrong call at the beginning, which was so difficult and I could see everyone just pulling away," Hamilton said.
"I thought that was kind of race over for us, but I just kept my head down. The guys did a great job with the pit stops."
Antonelli held on to second from Hamilton in the closing laps.
"Today was the maximum we could have done... On our side, a lot of work to do," Antonelli said.
"We've been struggling a bit more than usual, but still really happy to come away with P2."
The last four laps were a straight shootout for podium places after a lengthy safety car period and that was when Hamilton, who had been chasing Red Bull's Isack Hadjar for several laps, made his move.
Charles Leclerc, who had also been closer to the back of the grid at the start of the race amid the chaos of a wet track, salvaged fourth for Ferrari when he overtook Hadjar with two laps to go.
Hadjar finished fifth ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Liam Lawson was seventh while Fernando Alonso was eighth for Aston Martin, their best result of the season.
FIRST WET RACE OF 2026 The season had not yet had a wet race where the 2026 cars could be tested and the rain - which had stayed away in practice and qualifying - arrived with heavy showers sweeping across the circuit, delaying the start.
After a suspended start procedure, the second start had drivers split between intermediate and slick tyres but it was the former that thrived early in the race.
When the lights went out, Antonelli accelerated through the middle from third on the grid to take the lead from Verstappen while Russell shot past on the outside to move up from seventh to second.
But Verstappen's recovery began on lap six when he attacked Russell, overtaking the Briton by diving down the inside of turn four to set his sights on Antonelli.
The Italian had to defend his position until lap 10 when Valtteri Bottas spun his Cadillac into the gravel, bringing out the safety car as Verstappen pitted while the two Mercedes cars double stacked to switch to slick tyres.
VERSTAPPEN TAKES LEAD When the safety car came in, Verstappen stayed glued to Antonelli's rear tyre before overtaking the Italian on turn three, with Russell also surging past his team mate on the next turn to flip the order.
Verstappen looked comfortable setting the pace up front as he set fastest laps and extended his lead over Russell to over four seconds as a frustrated Antonelli informed the team that he had the pace to chase the Dutchman.
An impatient Antonelli overtook Russell on lap 21 to move up to second while behind them Hamilton had quietly been chipping away on his ageing soft tyres to move up to fifth behind Hadjar.
But Antonelli missed his braking point at turn 15 and went briefly off track, hitting the pit lane bollard and costing him valuable time as Verstappen extended his lead to eight seconds.
When the second safety car came out towards the end for Alex Albon's Williams that was stuck in the gravel, Russell suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he got out of the car with a suspected power unit issue.

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday for his first victory of the season after the race start was delayed by more than 90 minutes due to treacherous conditions at the Sepang International Circuit.
Verstappen was the last driver to win in Sepang in 2017 before it was taken off the calendar and the Dutchman, who had also taken pole, gave Red Bull a first victory with their own power unit despite an early setback when he lost the lead before turn one.
"It's a really nice one after the year that we've had and the progression that we've made. So I'm incredibly proud of everyone. It is super nice to win here," said Verstappen.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second for Mercedes and now has an 84-point lead over his closest rival and teammate George Russell, who was third when he retired with a suspected power unit issue with five laps remaining.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished third despite a tyre gamble that had dropped the Briton down to 18th at the start of the race.
"Obviously, we had the wrong call at the beginning, which was so difficult and I could see everyone just pulling away," Hamilton said.
"I thought that was kind of race over for us, but I just kept my head down. The guys did a great job with the pit stops."
Antonelli held on to second from Hamilton in the closing laps.
"Today was the maximum we could have done... On our side, a lot of work to do," Antonelli said.
"We've been struggling a bit more than usual, but still really happy to come away with P2."
The last four laps were a straight shootout for podium places after a lengthy safety car period and that was when Hamilton, who had been chasing Red Bull's Isack Hadjar for several laps, made his move.
Charles Leclerc, who had also been closer to the back of the grid at the start of the race amid the chaos of a wet track, salvaged fourth for Ferrari when he overtook Hadjar with two laps to go.
Hadjar finished fifth ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Liam Lawson was seventh while Fernando Alonso was eighth for Aston Martin, their best result of the season.
FIRST WET RACE OF 2026
The season had not yet had a wet race where the 2026 cars could be tested and the rain - which had stayed away in practice and qualifying - arrived with heavy showers sweeping across the circuit, delaying the start.
After a suspended start procedure, the second start had drivers split between intermediate and slick tyres but it was the former that thrived early in the race.
When the lights went out, Antonelli accelerated through the middle from third on the grid to take the lead from Verstappen while Russell shot past on the outside to move up from seventh to second.
But Verstappen's recovery began on lap six when he attacked Russell, overtaking the Briton by diving down the inside of turn four to set his sights on Antonelli.
The Italian had to defend his position until lap 10 when Valtteri Bottas spun his Cadillac into the gravel, bringing out the safety car as Verstappen pitted while the two Mercedes cars double stacked to switch to slick tyres.
VERSTAPPEN TAKES LEAD
When the safety car came in, Verstappen stayed glued to Antonelli's rear tyre before overtaking the Italian on turn three, with Russell also surging past his team mate on the next turn to flip the order.
Verstappen looked comfortable setting the pace up front as he set fastest laps and extended his lead over Russell to over four seconds as a frustrated Antonelli informed the team that he had the pace to chase the Dutchman.
An impatient Antonelli overtook Russell on lap 21 to move up to second while behind them Hamilton had quietly been chipping away on his ageing soft tyres to move up to fifth behind Hadjar.
But Antonelli missed his braking point at turn 15 and went briefly off track, hitting the pit lane bollard and costing him valuable time as Verstappen extended his lead to eight seconds.
When the second safety car came out towards the end for Alex Albon's Williams that was stuck in the gravel, Russell suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he got out of the car with a suspected power unit issue.

Source: Reuters

items.title: OPEC+ agrees to keep November oil output targets steady
items.author: Ahmad Ghaddar, Alex Lawler, Olesya Astakhova
items.creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Alex Lawler, Olesya Astakhova
items.summary: OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November at a meeting on Sunday, the producer group said, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year.
items.body:
OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November at a meeting on Sunday, the producer group said, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year.
Seven core members of the group comprising the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia made the decision for November in a brief online meeting on Sunday. The core members are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.
Gulf OPEC+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran , with exports fluctuating at 60% to 80% of normal levels in recent months.
"The OPEC+ group of seven kept their production ceilings unchanged, in line with market expectations. That said, despite rising flows through the Strait of Hormuz, their output levels remain well below quota," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo.
"Consequently, the oil market remains tight."
Oil prices had dropped on Friday after European leaders agreed to US President Donald Trump's request to release diesel reserves. Even so, Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel, up from about $73 before the Iran war started in late February.
OUTPUT HIKES HAVE BEEN LARGELY ON PAPER THIS YEAR The Iran war has also delayed the group's output [USN:L6N45O0QD TEXT:"capacity review"] — crucial to determine members’ 2027 output quotas — because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources told Reuters last week.
OPEC+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases stayed on paper because of the Middle East conflict.
The seven core OPEC+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February, OPEC data shows.
The seven hold their next meeting on November 1.
OPEC+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs the result of the capacity review to decide how to distribute increases and any [USN:L6N43U0TI TEXT:"changes to output are unlikely"] before 2027, sources have said.
A separate OPEC+ ministerial group called the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC), which does not decide policy, also met on Sunday to review the market.

items.title: US Supreme Court to kick off term with bid by Big Oil to toss climate suits
items.author: John Kruzel, Andrew Chung
items.creator: John Kruzel, Andrew Chung
items.summary: Monday's arguments mark the latest example of energy-sector companies asking the justices to block climate-related liability or limit federal environmental regulation.
items.body:
The US Supreme Court begins its new nine-month term on Monday with arguments in [USN:L1N45G0O2 TEXT:"a major case"] involving a bid by oil companies ExxonMobil (XOM.N) and Suncor Energy (SU.TO) to scuttle a lawsuit by officials in Boulder, Colorado, seeking monetary damages for harms caused by climate change.
It is the first of several important cases already teed up for the term, with disputes involving issues such as President Donald Trump 's [USN:S0N43101E TEXT:"immigration policies"] and state-level bans on [USN:S0N3YR01V TEXT:"assault-style rifles"] to be heard in the coming months. The court's 6-3 conservative majority has moved US law dramatically rightward in recent years.
The top US judicial body, as is its custom, opens its term on the first Monday in October.
US-based Exxon and Canada-based Suncor appealed after the Colorado Supreme Court let Boulder's lawsuit accusing them of state law violations proceed. The Trump administration has backed Exxon and Suncor, arguing that federal law precludes Boulder's claims.
Boulder's city and county governments have accused the two companies of helping drive climate change and misleading the public about the risks of fossil fuels. Boulder aims to hold the companies liable for past and future costs associated with climate change such as infrastructure repairs, environmental damage, emergency management and harms to public health.
The burning of fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases including carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, trapping heat and raising average global temperatures over time.
Nearly 60 state and local governments have brought similar suits seeking billions of dollars from fossil fuel companies, with more continuing to be filed, Exxon and Suncor told the justices. A ruling by the Supreme Court in favor of the companies could lead to many of those cases being dismissed.
Monday's arguments mark the latest example of energy-sector companies asking the justices to block climate-related liability or limit federal environmental regulation.
Backers of the oil companies argue that if Boulder's most far-reaching claims are allowed to proceed, it could give states sweeping power over conduct occurring far outside their borders.
Energy companies and trade groups, along with states allied with them, have built a largely winning record before the justices over the past two decades in cases involving climate liability and the reach of federal environmental regulation.
Exxon and Suncor argue, among other things, that Boulder's claims intrude on an area governed by the Clean Air Act.
Justice Samuel Alito [USN:L1N45K0QH TEXT:"has recused"] himself from participating in the case. Alito owns stock in several oil and gas companies but not Exxon or Suncor, according to his financial disclosure forms.
The Supreme Court's decision is expected by the end of June.

items.title: Brazilians head to polls in high-stakes, polarized election
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, is seeking a fourth term as president while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power.
items.body:
Brazilians queued in long lines to vote on Sunday in the first round of a tight election, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling.
The field of 13 candidates has been led by two clear frontrunners — leftist [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva"], 80, who is seeking a fourth term, and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power.
A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's reelection could create a headache for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.
Despite growing worries over the public finances and sluggish economic growth of Brazil , the campaign has offered [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"meager policy debate"], as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.
If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes, the top two will face off on October 25. Surveys show Lula and Flavio polling roughly even in a likely runoff.
UNDECIDED VOTERS While polls right up until Saturday showed Lula would likely lead the first round but not avoid a runoff, Flavio told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was confident he could win the presidency in the first round, citing voters' frustration with his chief opponent.
Flavio was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula," he said. "I hope it’s enough to secure a victory in the first round."
Some voters told Reuters their voting intentions supported Flavio's tactics.
"My main goal is to get the (Workers' Party) out," said Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer living in Sao Paulo, on her way to her polling station.
"I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.
Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Flavio despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.
"We need to remove Lula because he is destroying the country," Tempel said.
OUTSIDE INTERFERENCE On the other hand, Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to [USN:L6N43R03C TEXT:"send US officials to Brazil"].
"What is at stake is the future of Brazil," Lula said after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.
Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.
"Elections are never easy and you know that there is a very strong campaign of the far-right wanting to dominate everything, including with foreign influence, wanting to get in the way. We are confident in our President Lula, who will fight for national sovereignty," said Pedro Palacio, 45, who was voting in the capital Brasilia alongside his wife, Andreia, and their two sons and two dogs, all of whom were decked out in outfits supporting Lula.
Federal police have opened an initial investigation into foreign interference after receiving a report from the Solicitor General's Office, the federal police chief said in a press conference.
"It hasn’t become a formal inquiry yet; it is already an ongoing investigation, but the official order establishing the police inquiry has not yet been issued," said Andrei Rodrigues, head of the federal police.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"alleged US and Russian interference"] before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs.
ECONOMIC HEADWINDS Despite [USN:L1N44111S TEXT:"falling inequality"] and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity.
Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.
Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president may need to address. The government lowered its [USN:L1N45E0QC TEXT:"economic growth forecasts"] for this year and next to just 2.0% and 2.3% respectively.
SCANDAL-PLAGUED CAMPAIGN Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil's political class and renewed public anger over corruption.
Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker's ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Flavio Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police.
The senator has denied any wrongdoing, although he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Vorcaro to make a movie about his father.
The banker's connections to Moraes, widely perceived as a Lula ally, [USN:L6N44U1B6 TEXT:"plunged the court into crisis"] a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the president. Moraes has said the case against him is politically motivated for his role in the [USN:L1N45711X TEXT:"conviction of the elder Bolsonaro"].
On Sunday, voters will also elect all 513 lower house members and two-thirds of the Senate, where some lawmakers have pushed to impeach Moraes.
Congress has gained greater influence in Brazilian politics since the impeachment of former President Dilma Rousseff, a Lula ally, in 2016, raising the stakes of those legislative races.

items.title: “It never occurred to me that he wouldn’t do it”: Aaron Sorkin on Jesse Eisenberg's refusal to work in ''The Social Reckoning'
items.summary: Actor-director Aaron Sorkin admitted that "it never occured" to him that the actor Jesse Eisenberg wouldn’t be on board for the movie 'The Social Reckoning', which is a sequel to 'The Social Network,' ...
items.body:
“It never occurred to me that he wouldn’t do it”: Aaron Sorkin on Jesse Eisenberg's refusal to work in ''The Social Reckoning' Actor-director Aaron Sorkin admitted that "it never occured" to him that the actor Jesse Eisenberg wouldn’t be on board for the movie 'The Social Reckoning', which is a sequel to 'The Social Network,' in which he portrayed the young tech billionaire, reported Variety. 
ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 22:29 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 22:29 IST

Aaron Sorkin and Jesse Eisenberg (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Actor-director Aaron Sorkin admitted that "it never occured" to him that the actor Jesse Eisenberg wouldn’t be on board for the movie 'The Social Reckoning', which is a sequel to 'The Social Network,' in which he portrayed the young tech billionaire, reported Variety. Speaking with Entertainment Weekly, as quoted by Variety, Sorkin recounted that he was “just a couple of pages from being done with the script for the new film when he ran into Eisenberg at a party and said, ‘I’m gonna be sending you something in a couple of weeks.’”
The actor “smiled and nodded, and I sent it to him,” said Sorkin. “It never occurred to me that he wouldn’t wanna do it,” as quoted by Variety. Sorkin continued, explaining he tried to convince Eisenberg, but he didn’t budge.
“This is the only time I’ve written myself an outline. I don’t do it for the movies, but I did it for my conversations with Jesse. It was arguments for why he should do it. They included, ‘We already know you’re gonna be great because you were already once.’ You know, ‘Here are the great moments that you’re gonna get to play in the movie.’ And I laid it out for him.” And while Eisenberg didn’t sign on, he did tell Sorkin that their conversations made him “come closer to changing my mind than I thought you were going to,” which the director said 'pleased' him," added Sorkin as quoted by Variety. Not even a sizeable paycheck could sway Eisenberg, admitted Sorkin.
“I knew what the studio was offering him to do it, but money does not motivate Jesse. It’s infuriating. If anything, money is a disincentive for him. It’s admirable. He’s very concerned about raising his kids with too much money,” said Sorkin, as quoted by Variety. In the lead-up to the release of “The Social Reckoning,” which hits theatres on October 9, Eisenberg’s refusal to return as Zuckerberg has been a hot topic.
Earlier, while speaking with Variety, Jesse Eisenberg said, “I just told [Sorkin] I’m moving in different directions in my life, and you know, what he said sums it up nicely. I don’t want to be associated with that character, but all of my reasons for not wanting to do the movie have nothing to do with how wonderful the movie is, and will be, and I’m sure is already.” 'The Social Network,' which also starred Andrew Garfield and Justin Timberlake, was nominated for eight Oscars and won three, including best adapted screenplay for Sorkin, best film editing and best original score. Eisenberg earned an Oscar nomination for his portrayal of Zuckerberg.
'The Social Reckoning' stars Strong, Mikey Madison, Jeremy Allen White, Billy Magnussen, Bill Burr and more. (ANI)
