items.title: Like a 'vertical roller coaster': Simulating flight FZ1073's sudden plunge
items.author: Ben Makori
items.creator: Ben Makori
items.summary: A prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe, an expert says.
items.body:
Flydubai's [USN:S8N44D013 TEXT:"flight FZ1073"], which plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, would have felt like a "vertical roller coaster", according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.
The steep fall, after an attack on the captain by the co-pilot during a flight on Wednesday, would have put huge strain on the Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft - as well as the passengers and crew, said Alberto Paduanelli, owner of ALPA Simulation in Sherfield on Loddon, southern England.
The co-pilot of the flydubai jet, which was bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"terrorist attack"]".
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, two sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity. Reuters could not independently reach al-Hammami for comment.
Flydubai says the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation and it cannot comment further. Oman has yet to comment on the incident.
"A plunge of 16,000 feet (4,877 metres) over 30 seconds will feel like you are over on a very, very vertical roller coaster," Paduanelli said, sitting at the controls of the simulator cockpit.
"The difference is that on the roller coaster, you know what's happening," he said, adding that with a sudden drop "you feel the negative g-force on your body".
For passengers who are not strapped in, "Your body will literally lift from the seat", he said.
Using a simulator to recreate the incident, Paduanelli said the aircraft's autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing the jet to accelerate rapidly.
US President Donald Trump has praised the Boeing jet for withstanding the severe forces put on it during the incident. The plane was levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, before a reserve crew of pilots onboard landed the plane.
"It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural planning and design," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that the 737 Max "was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do".
Boeing did not respond to a request for comment.
Aircraft are designed and tested to withstand substantial aerodynamic loads, but Paduanelli said a prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe.
"This was nothing but a miracle that nothing was hurt apart from the captain, unfortunately, and that two pilots were onboard," Paduanelli said.
Details about al-Hammami's past have trickled out.
Royal Air Maroc told Reuters he did a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. Buckinghamshire New University in Britain said he did a distance-learning course in aviation management with the institution, but no pilot training.
An Australian Federal Police spokesperson said on Sunday that authorities there were investigating al-Hammami's "links to Australia". A source briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne.

Oct 4 : Croatia's Luka Modric said he was ashamed of his side's performance after they lost 7-0 to England in Rijeka on Saturday, the heaviest defeat in their history.
Croatia's previous heaviest loss was a 6-0 defeat by Spain in 2018. Modric, the country's most-capped player, said the manner of the defeat by England was unacceptable.
"It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance without duels, fouls, aggressiveness, togetherness... I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time I feel ashamed after a game," he told Jutarnji.
"You can lose, or play against an opponent who is better - and they are right now. But in any case, losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable.

items.title: Two dead in flooding in Spain's Catalonia region
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.
items.body:
Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.
Catalan leader Salvador Illa confirmed the death of a man after a wall collapsed in Tordera, a town to the north of Barcelona, in a message on his social media account on Sunday.
Another person died in Montornès del Vallès, firefighters said on Sunday, while emergency services were searching for a missing person in Pineda de Mar, a town 52 km (32 miles) to the north of Barcelona.
Catalan authorities issued a red alert warning and urged people to stay inside from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Saturday until Sunday at 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) because a "mini-hurricane" could hit the northeastern region, with more heavy rain forecast.
Homes were flooded and cars left submerged in Bellvitge and Cornella near Barcelona after torrential rain on Saturday. Ducks swam in huge puddles that formed on motorways in Barcelona.
Sarai Sarroca, director of regional weather service Meteocat, said on Saturday that the core of an exceptional weather system was over the Mediterranean and a "mini-hurricane" could move over land in Catalonia.
Flights were cancelled or delayed at Barcelona airport, La Vanguardia newspaper reported on Saturday.
All local trains were disrupted by the deluge. Shops shut early, football matches were called off and a performance of Verdi's Aida at Barcelona's Liceu opera house was cancelled.

FAST

PHUKET: The United States aircraft carrier George H W Bush arrived in Thailand's resort island of Phuket on Sunday (Oct 4) with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East.

For the last six months, the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier and its strike group supported Operation Epic Fury and the US naval blockade in the US Central Command area of responsibility to secure maritime security and stability in the Middle East, according to the US Navy.

Phuket is the first port call for the George H W Bush Carrier Strike Group since departing Norfolk, Virginia, and Mayport, Florida, in March, the US Navy said in a statement.

Sailors will take part in cultural and community activities in Phuket, including sightseeing tours and a US-Thailand soccer match, it said.

The carrier anchored offshore, while crew members are expected to come ashore through Phuket Deep Sea Port and spend time on the popular southern resort island from Oct 4 to 9, local media reported.

Some sailors were seen coming ashore by boat.

The visit follows a five-day port call by the US carrier Abraham Lincoln at Laem Chabang in eastern Thailand last month, with about 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard.

A local mayor had estimated each US service member from the Lincoln could spend up to 3,000 baht ($89) per day during the visit.

Thailand is the United States' only treaty ally in mainland Southeast Asia.

items.title: Uflex, US firm Spectra enters race for proposed polymer banknote programme
items.author: Press Trust of India
items.summary: The programme was initiated by Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Pvt Ltd (BRBNMPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India ...
items.body: Homegrown polymer science firm Uflex, in partnership with the US-based Spectra Systems, has submitted bids for the proposed polymer banknote programme as the RBI evaluates potential suppliers to manufacture polymer-based currency substrate, sources said.The programme was initiated by Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Pvt Ltd (BRBNMPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).As per the tender document, it seeks Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP), coated uniformly with opacifying ink to the required colour, along with an anti-static coating, to provide a good surface for printing and ink adhesion. It requires 68,000 reams, 34,000 each for ₹10 and 20 denominations.Polymer (plastic) currency is used fully or partially by around 60 countries.Australia was the first to introduce it in 1988. Other major nations that use polymer banknotes include the United Kingdom, Canada, New Zealand, Singapore, Vietnam, and Romania.The tender was floated on July 17, with August 18 as the last date for submission of expressions of interest (EOI). The tender was floated after the government's approval to introduce polymer currency on a trial basis.According to sources, a joint proposal from Uflex and US-based Spectra Systems has submitted a bid in the tender.A query sent to Uflex seeking comment on its participation in the EOI remained unanswered.The RBI, with the recommendation of its Central Board, had sent a proposal to the government in terms of Section 25 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, for introduction of one billion pieces each of ₹10 and ₹20 polymer banknotes for field trials and for regular issuance of polymer banknotes in these two denominations after successful completion of field trials, Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary said in a reply to the Lok Sabha on July 27.The proposal has been approved by the government, he stated.The introduction of polymer banknotes is currently in a preliminary phase and the impact on digital payments, if any, could be ascertained only after regular issuance of these notes. Moreover, banknotes and digital payment systems are complementary payment tools available to the public, he added.The proposed programme is expected to involve technical evaluation and testing of substrate samples before the larger procurement process. The assessment is likely to examine aspects such as security features, manufacturing consistency, scalability and long-term supply capabilities.The Uflex-Spectra partnership brings together Uflex's polymer manufacturing and industrial capabilities with Spectra Systems' expertise in banknote authentication and security technologies, they added.The proposed programme comes as India evaluates the feasibility of polymer-based currency substrates and the industrial capabilities required to manufacture them at scale.In June, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that a proposal to introduce polymer currency notes was under consideration by the central bank and was at a preliminary stage.

items.title: Éthiopie-La capitale du Tigré sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
items.body:
Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
Les Forces de paix du Tigré, une milice pro-gouvernementale dit dans un message publié sur Facebook que ses combattants avaient pris le contrôle de Mekelle, la capitale du Tigré.
Une source proche de la milice avait auparavant dit à Reuters qu'elle était entrée dans le centre-ville samedi après-midi, suivie par l'armée éthiopienne.
Le Front populaire de libération du Tigré (TPLF), qui dirige l'alliance d'opposition, a dit de son côté dans un communiqué publié sur Facebook qu'il s'était retiré de Mekelle, et que le gouvernement régional serait "temporairement transféré hors de Mekelle et opérerait depuis un autre endroit".
Une source humanitaire et un habitant de Mekelle, sous couvert d'anonymat, ont confirmé que la ville était désormais aux mains des forces gouvernementales.
Le cabinet du Premier ministre Abiy Ahmed n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire.
La prise de Mekelle par les forces pro-gouvernementales constitue une importante perte pour l'alliance d'opposition dirigée par le TPLF, qui avait lancé une vaste [USN:L8N45F0T4 TEXT:"offensive"] le 23 septembre contre l'armée éthiopienne.
Les forces fédérales éthiopiennes et les combattants alliés ont lancé une contre-offensive rapide dans le Tigré, mais selon les analystes, ces combats — qui constituent la pire escalade depuis la guerre civile de 2020-2022 — risquent de dégénérer en un conflit régional plus vaste.
Le gouvernement fédéral d'Addis-Abeba a rompu ses relations diplomatiques avec l'Érythrée la semaine dernière, l'accusant de soutenir l'alliance rebelle aux côtés du Soudan et de l'Égypte. Les trois pays rejettent ces accusations.

Oct 4 (Reuters) – Ethiopian government forces and allied militias have regained control of the capital of Tigray, three sources told Reuters on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern region.

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the opposition alliance, said in a statement posted on Facebook it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be “temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else.”

A source close to the pro-government militia, the Tigray Peace Forces, said its fighters entered the centre of Mekelle on Saturday afternoon, followed by the Ethiopian military. A humanitarian source and a Mekelle resident, who asked not to be named, confirmed the city was controlled by government forces.

Show Full Article

The prime minister’s office did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

LOSS OF MEKELLE A MAJOR BLOW FOR TPLF

The taking of Mekelle by pro-government forces is a major loss for the opposition alliance led by the TPLF, which launched a big offensive on September 23 against the Ethiopian military.

Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have made a quick counterattack into Tigray, but analysts say the fighting — the worst escalation since a 2020-2022 civil war — threatens to escalate into a wider regional conflict.

The federal government in Addis Ababa severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea last week, accusing it of supporting the rebel alliance alongside Sudan and Egypt. The three countries deny this.

(Reporting by Ammu Kannampillay; Editing by Silvia Aloisi and Helen Popper)

A new White House task force will produce a report assessing risks posed by artificial intelligence and what responsibility the US federal government should have over the technology.

The task force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, the Wall Street Journal reported, adding he confirmed his role to the paper. It makes Clayton effectively the Trump administration’s new AI czar, a senior White House official told the Wall Street Journal.

“The president asked that a group be put together that was going to ensure exactly what he said, which is that we stay the leaders in superintelligence, and that the interests of the American people are put first,” the Journal cited Clayton as saying. A White House official confirmed the Journal report.

Show Full Article

Despite growing concerns about security risks posed by AI, President Donald Trump has spurned calls for new regulations. Instead, he has prioritized keeping the US ahead of China and backed a voluntary framework involving outside safety audits and stronger internal controls.

“We have a very big lead, and we’re going to keep our lead, and it’s a very positive thing,” the president said during a meeting with industry executives this week.

The task force has been named the “Super Intelligence Force,” Trump’s preferred name for AI, and will have 120 days to prepare the report, the report said.

Separately, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized prominent AI leaders’ warnings about existential risks posed by the technology as alarmist and unhelpful, calling on the industry to police itself and produce solutions.

“It is the people at the labs who have to accept responsibility, and I agree with that,” Bessent said in an Axios interview published Saturday. “I think the labs have come around to that way of thinking, too.”

–With assistance from Kate Sullivan.

(Adds White House response in third paragraph)

items.title: Rare police raid of Taipei gay bar sparks angry protest
items.author: Yimou Lee, Ann Wang
items.creator: Yimou Lee, Ann Wang
items.summary: Taipei police took in 51 people in for questioning and arrested the bar's owner.
items.body:
Around 100 members of Taipei's LGBTQ+ community protested on Sunday after police raided a gay bar the day before and detained its customers, a highly unusual move given that Taiwan prides itself on its liberal image and legal support for sexual minorities.
Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019 in a first for Asia and is normally a bastion of tolerance in a region where LGBTQ+ rights are often either suppressed or outlawed.
Taipei holds its main [USN:L4N3W50AF TEXT:"Pride"] event later this month, the largest in East Asia.
Taipei police raided the Commander D gay bar in the city's Wanhua district on Saturday afternoon, taking 51 people in for questioning, and arresting the bar's owner. Reuters could not reach him for comment.
Precinct spokesperson Chen Yu-cheng told Reuters police had acted on a search warrant for suspected "offences against public morality".
Chen said the 51 people were suspected of violating a law that prohibits "wantonly exposing one's naked body or presenting a lascivious posture in a public place or publicly accessible place".
Protesters marched peacefully but noisily to the precinct police station on Sunday afternoon.
"They raided the place violently. It was very scary," one of those detained, who asked to be identified only by his family name Wen, told Reuters.
The Taipei city government referred Reuters to a separate police statement, which said police received a complaint alleging that the bar could be violating public decency laws.
Mayor Chiang Wan-an from the main opposition party, the Kuomintang, who faces an election next month, has previously attended Taipei Pride and expressed his support for the LGBTQ+ community.
The precinct chief, who did not give his name, came out to speak to protesters briefly.
"We respect the culture of a pluralistic society and will protect the rights of every citizen," he said, as protesters shouted their disapproval at him.
Protester Kang Yang said he was angry the raid had happened, particularly during Pride month.
"I'm not cool with this," he said. "This city used to claim that it was queer friendly."
Taiwan was under martial law until 1987 and same-sex relations were a largely taboo issue at the time.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the opposition alliance, said in a statement it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be "temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else".
A humanitarian source and a Mekelle resident, who asked not to be named, confirmed the city was in the hands of government forces and their allies.
LOSS OF MEKELLE A MAJOR BLOW FOR TPLF The taking of Mekelle by pro-government forces is a major loss for the opposition alliance led by the TPLF, which [USN:L6N45G0U0 TEXT:"launched a big offensive"] on September 23 against the Ethiopian military.
Ethiopian federal forces have made a quick counterattack into Tigray, but analysts say the fighting — the worst escalation since a 2020-2022 civil war — threatens to escalate into a wider regional conflict.
The federal government in Addis Ababa severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea last week, accusing it of supporting the rebel alliance alongside Sudan and Egypt.
Egypt's foreign minister denied backing the TPLF and its allies. "I have to be very clear, we are not party to the domestic crisis facing Ethiopia now. It has nothing to do with us," Badr Abdelatty told Reuters on Sunday. Eritrea and Sudan also deny helping the rebels.
Abdelatty was speaking ahead of a meeting between Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and his Eritrean and Somali counterparts in Egypt on Sunday. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, the head of Sudan’s army, was also due to attend the talks.
Egypt and Ethiopia, two of Africa’s most populous countries, have been at loggerheads for years over Ethiopia’s construction of a major dam on the Nile River, which Egypt views as a threat to its water security.
“It is an existential issue. It’s life or death for 110 million people,” Abdelatty said.
items.raw_description: Pro-government forces have regained control of the capital of Tigray, they said on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern Ethiopian region.

items.title: Saudi Arabia quietly shelving NEOM Stadium, one of 2034 World Cup venues
items.author: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.summary: It was meant to be one of the most ambitious venues for the 2034 FIFA World Cup.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it.
The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM.
NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil.
Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was [USN:S8N40J01E TEXT:"no longer a priority"], and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled.
However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely.
NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority.
The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction.
RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format.
Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities.
MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters.
According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold".
The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033.
Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis.
Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it [USN:L1N45M0WE TEXT:"expected"] a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6% following a drop in oil activities.
PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added.
In January Reuters [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"reported"] that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba.
Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy [USN:L1N40Y0DC TEXT:"later articulated"] by Saudi officials.
Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The [USN:L6N43I0ZY TEXT:"Aramco Stadium"] in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale.
Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

items.title: Los 10 objetos más olvidados en Uber México: los teléfonos lideran
items.author: Isaac Garrido
items.summary: El Índice de Objetos Olvidados de la plataforma destaca que también se han olvidado una canasta de tacos y hasta un penacho.
items.body: “Creo que lo dejé en el Uber…”. Si usas este servicio es posible que hayas olvidado algo después de un viaje. Y esto es tan frecuente que la compañía lanza desde hace 10 años su Índice de Objetos Olvidados. En su edición 2026, los teléfonos lideran el listado como el artículo que más dejan los pasajeros en México. Las carteras y bolsos están el segundo puesto, mientras que las llaves ocuparon el tercer lugar. Otros artículos de la lista incluyen audífonos y bocinas, ropa, lentes, dinero en efectivo y hasta computadoras. Pero además de los artículos cotidianos, el informe también registró objetos inusuales que han sido encontrados por los conductores como un penacho, un tambor africano y hasta 400 tacos de canasta, que tradicionalmente se colocan y transportan dentro de un cesto para mantenerlos calientes. También se han dejado carriolas, extensiones de cabello y hasta prótesis dentales. Elaborado a partir de los reportes de usuarios que dejan cosas, el Índice también rastrea los días en los que más se olvidan ciertos artículos. Los martes y viernes son “los días oficiales” para olvidar laptops, los miércoles suelen ser comunes para dejar cargadores de computadora y los lentes se dejan los lunes, jueves, sábado y domingo. El informe también registra los horarios en los que los clientes tienden a ser más olvidadizos. Los lunes el pico de olvidos ocurre entre 2 PM y 4PM y de 6PM a 8PM. Los viernes entre 7 y 9PM. Los sábados tiene un punto crítico a las 3 PM y de 7 a 10 PM. La madrugada del domingo también concentra muchas de las pérdidas. Si las situaciones anteriores te resultan familiares y dejaste algo en tu Uber , así puedes recuperarlo:

items.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Additional points remain to be communicated to the US, a foreign-ministry spokesperson said.
items.body:
The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven Iranian conditions set out in a June interim agreement with the US are met, state media reported Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf as saying on Sunday.
Iran presented a proposal during the UN General Assembly under which the Strait of Hormuz waterway could be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days if the conditions were met, with the US replying to this proposal last week via Qatari intermediaries.
"The position of the Islamic Republic of Iran is completely clear and firm, and the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until our seven conditions, based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met," Qalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, was quoted as saying.
He said Washington "must understand that the period of dragging out the (diplomatic) process and dictating one-sided demands is over".
IRAN SAYS NO NUCLEAR DISCUSSIONS A Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had clarified its broad positions via mediators to the US response but that additional points remained to be communicated to Washington.
"The Americans' propositions are more or less in line with their previous positions, specifically on the nuclear issue. We told them our focus in this stage is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz and the return to security in this waterway requires clear steps from the US," spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said.
He also denied Tehran had offered UN nuclear watchdog inspections of its nuclear facilities in exchange for US sanctions relief, saying Iran had not entered into nuclear discussions with Washington.
The [USN:L1N45M06A TEXT:"document being circulated"] outlines a seven-day period of trust-building aimed at returning the two sides to an enhanced version of the memorandum of understanding agreed in June, including concrete steps on Iran's nuclear programme, an official briefed on the talks said last week.
The disagreement centres on the sequencing of the steps rather than the components of the plan, the official added.
WARNING FROM ARAQCHI Qatar has been shuttling messages between Washington and Tehran in an effort to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war that began at the end of February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran.
The June memorandum of understanding led to a brief ceasefire and included provisions on the strait and Iran's nuclear programme.
Separately, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told foreign ambassadors and diplomats in Tehran on Sunday that Tehran hoped Washington would choose diplomacy but warned that Iran was prepared to respond if the US again chose military action.
On Thursday, sources told Reuters that Iran was preparing a [USN:L8N45M1N4 TEXT:"broader and more forceful response"] if Washington resumed large-scale military attacks.
“If they again move towards military solutions, we are more prepared than before and will take whatever action is necessary to defend ourselves,” Araqchi said on Sunday.
Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia told Fars news agency on Sunday Iran would upgrade the range of its missiles.

items.title: Latvian PM on track to lead pro-Ukraine coalition after election win
items.author: Andrius Sytas
items.creator: Andrius Sytas
items.summary: Andris Kulbergs has promised to improve governance and reduce public spending.
items.body:
Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs was set to retain power and form a pro-Ukrainian coalition after his centrist United List secured the biggest [USN:L8N45O1BP TEXT:"parliamentary election"] victory since Latvia regained independence in 1991.
With 97% of ballots counted after Saturday's election in the NATO and European Union country bordering Russia, United List was on 35.3%, enough for 42 seats in the 100-seat parliament.
A businessman and amateur rally driver, Kulbergs, 47, came to power in May after the previous coalition crumbled over its handling of incidents in which stray [USN:L8N41K055 TEXT:"Ukrainian military drones"] flew undetected into Latvia.
Latvia's economy has underperformed its Baltic neighbours for more than a decade and Kulbergs has vowed to improve governance, cut red tape and reduce public spending, political scientist Roberts Kits said.
"Kulbergs played on being a get-things-done type of guy and has persuaded the voters that he can do things differently, bring some fresh energy," he said.
"This means the responsibility is huge. People expect him to deliver, but the question remains whether he has the team to do it."
United List appeared able to secure a parliamentary majority with either the nationalist National Alliance or the liberal Progressives, Kits said.
"(Kulbergs) is smart, let's hope that something will be better, that he will change what can be changed", Aina Sturmane, 78, a pensioner, told Reuters in Riga on Sunday.
No Latvian government has survived a full term, and Kulbergs will face an uphill battle holding together the United List, a loose alliance of small parties and independents, said political scientist Janis Ikstens.
PM PLEDGES TO MAINTAIN HARD LINE ON RUSSIA Kulbergs pledged continuing support to Ukraine and to keep a hard line towards Moscow.
"Any economic ties with Russia makes us weak. Yes, it can bring some extra money, but it's a weakness Russia might exploit," he told reporters at his party's headquarters on election night as supporters celebrated the scale of the win.
"It's remarkably good. I was not expecting such a result," Kulbergs said.
Voter turnout was 51.8%, down from 59.4% in 2022, underscoring disappointment with politicians in Latvia, Ikstens said.
United List was followed by the populist, MAGA-style Latvia First, which was on 13.1%. Latvia First had courted the country's substantial ethnic Russian minority in the run-up to the vote.
Third in the ranking was the pro-Russian Sovereign Power party, on 11.7%, followed by the National Alliance, which promotes a hardline approach to the Kremlin, at 8.9%.
Throughout his campaign, Kulbergs promised more anti-drone capability for Latvia and to maintain defence spending at 5% of gross domestic product, one of the highest levels in NATO.
His pro-Kremlin rivals said Latvia should stop any aid to Ukraine and instead focus on tackling cost-of-living issues, particularly among the country's Russian-speaking minority.
Although pro-Russian parties increased their representation, Kits said they remained sidelined and were unlikely to influence government policy.
Latvia's ethnic Russian minority is split between those who oppose Moscow's war in Ukraine and others who voice frustration with policies at home aimed at limiting their influence on public life, which many of them see as discriminatory.
Latvia, with a population of 1.9 million, is sandwiched between the Baltic Sea and Russia and Belarus to the east, with EU and NATO allies Estonia and Lithuania to the north and south.

items.title: Haunted by grief, Gaza's displaced still wait overseas for return
items.author: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
items.creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
items.summary: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
items.body:
Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war that was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, and who remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their [USN:L1N45F09E TEXT:"destroyed homes"] and neighbourhoods.
"I left Gaza and came to Egypt, the land of Kinana (referring to Egypt), but at the same time, this will not be forgotten, my dear brother, it will not be forgotten," he said.
"I am waiting for the opportunity, I am waiting for the moment when Gaza becomes stable so I can return to my country, and be a productive member of this country, and be a positive force for the country."
Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza that was meant to start a process of reconstruction under a technocratic government along with a political process that would lead to an eventual full Israeli withdrawal, little has changed.
Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where Palestinians live, mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies and no prospect of reconstruction soon.
Some 308 members of Hassayna's [USN:L8N4400Z0 TEXT:"extended family"] were killed when Israeli strikes destroyed a cluster of Gaza City apartment buildings where they had gathered for shelter on November 22, 2023, according to Palestinian authorities.
Among those killed were his wife, four of their adult sons and four small grandchildren including an infant only a few months old.
Hassayna's oldest son Mohammed is also in Cairo along with his own four children, as is the widow of one of his dead sons with her daughter. He has brothers in the Egyptian capital too.
One daughter was medically evacuated to Turkey with her husband and six children, and another daughter remains in Gaza with her five children although her husband was killed in the attack.
The Israeli military did not respond to a request for comment on the details of the November 22 strike. It said its attacks in Gaza are directed at military targets, while trying to reduce harm to civilians.
ABOUT 7,000 PALESTINIANS HAVE RETURNED TO GAZA In August, Hassayna watched on video from Cairo as relatives buried 112 family members, including his wife, sons and grandchildren, whose bodies had been recovered from the rubble, with dozens still missing.
Hassayna owned a business selling tools for firefighting and safety equipment in Gaza and some of his goods survived the war. He periodically sells some to fund his stay in Cairo, where he has remarried.
All those who left Gaza were vetted before their departure by both Israel and Egypt, but many have found it hard to return to the territory.
Although some Israeli politicians have urged a policy of encouraging all Gaza's population to leave and to prevent those who left from returning, about 7,000 have gone home. Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza.
However, no widespread return of those who fled Gaza may be likely until the territory's prospects are clearer.
"If Gaza returns. If there is an international agreement (with) a comprehensive situation for the Palestinian people and construction begins, why would I delay?" he said.
items.raw_description: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.

items.title: Revolut's rise to become Europe's $115 billion big bank rival
items.author: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
items.creator: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
items.summary: Revolut has become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, though it faces hurdles.
items.body:
Revolut has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees.
Yet Revolut faces many hurdles itself, with the amount of revenue it extracts per customer a fraction of its established competitors and a small lending business by industry standards.
A spokesperson for Revolut said in an email that the London-based company has a "diversified business model", earning its revenue from various products and services rather than lending.
"That means our growth depends on building things customers value, rather than on interest rates," the spokesperson said.
Here's Revolut's rise, in five charts:
GOING FOR GLOBAL CEO Nik Storonsky has stressed he wants Revolut to be truly global, expanding into markets [USN:L4N44E0AO TEXT:"from Mexico to Australia"].
The company has announced several new licences in recent weeks, as it aims to become one of only a handful of banks with retail operations spanning so much of the globe.
Meanwhile, some traditional lenders seen as global, including HSBC (HSBA.L) , are reducing their retail footprint.
Valued at $115 billion privately, Revolut is now worth more than Britain's Barclays (BARC.L) and France's Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) as investors bet on its tech platform winning over more customers globally.
Revolut's 2025 pretax profit was £1.7 billion ($2.2 billion), a fraction of Barclays' £9 billion, but growing fast.
Paulo Macedo, CEO of Portugal's biggest bank, Caixa Geral de Depósitos, said in June that 2025 was the last year in which the 150-year-old bank would record higher profit than Revolut.
"When you go to Europe the bank CEOs there are talking about Revolut as their most important threat because of their aggressive marketing and growth," said Cihan Duran, director at S&P Global Ratings.
MARRED BY SETBACKS In the US, where Revolut has a provisional license, it will face tougher competition, investors said.
"The US could be potentially the biggest growth for Revolut. But at the same time, the US is the most competitive market," said Konstantin Sidorov, CEO of the London Technology Club, which invested in Revolut when it was valued at just $5.5 billion.
There have been setbacks, including a fine in Lithuania for failing to prevent money laundering. Revolut said an investigation had not identified any confirmed instances of money laundering, adding that it had signed a settlement with the central bank and taken steps to resolve shortcomings.
And in September, Revolut accidentally sent customer data to hackers posing as government investigators. The company said its systems and customer funds were unaffected and it had contacted the "limited number of impacted individuals" to give support.
In 2024 and 2025, Revolut was the most-complained-about bank in Britain in fraud cases whereby customers are tricked into sending cash to scammers, Ombudsman data compiled by consumer advocacy firm Which? showed.
Revolut has previously said in response it takes fraud very seriously and has robust customer protections in place.
CUSTOMERS HAVE SURGED A striking measure of its growth is customer numbers.
In Ireland, for example, Revolut said that 80% of the adult population has a Revolut account.
Revolut's website shows it has 80 million customers, against 84 million for JPMorgan (JPM.N) and 41 million for HSBC.
REVENUE-PER-CUSTOMER IS LOW Revolut makes far less from each of its customers than traditional banks, a Reuters analysis of its figures shows. Average deposit balances are also much lower.
Lower per-customer revenue is in part because Revolut lends much less than traditional banks, instead relying on fees such as card subscriptions.
With just £2.2 billion in loans at end-2025, Revolut's loan-to-deposit ratio of 6% compares with 55% for HSBC and 86% for Societe Generale.
Scaling its lending business will introduce risks including managing big and complex credit exposures, while entering fiercely competitive local mortgage markets will not be easy, analysts and investors said.
TOO FEW PRIMARY ACCOUNTS Revolut has attracted customers with its easy-to-use app but executives acknowledge too few use it as a primary bank account.
Revolut declined to comment in its latest results on how many customers did so in 2025, but said the figure was up 45% from a year ago.
This metric is a focus for Revolut's biggest backers.
Alex Immerman, an investor at Andreessen Horowitz, which is known as "a16z", told Reuters it was watching for primary-account adoption, as well as total customer balances.
($1 = 0.7573 pounds)
items.raw_description: Revolut has become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, though it faces hurdles.

items.title: Trump forms "Super Intelligence Force" to cement US dominance in next-gen AI
items.summary: In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, "Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where the World's most important Technology Companies came together, and confirmed their ...
items.body:
Trump forms "Super Intelligence Force" to cement US dominance in next-gen AI In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, "Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where the World's most important Technology Companies came together, and confirmed their responsibilities to the American People, I am announcing the formation of the Super Intelligence Force (SIF)."
ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 19:15 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 19:15 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump has announced the creation of a new federal task force called the Super Intelligence Force (SIF) to centralise executive branch policies and lead national efforts in advanced artificial intelligence. The announcement builds on the administration's executive order, which replaced the terms "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" with "Super Intelligence" and "SI" across all executive branch operations.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, "Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where the World's most important Technology Companies came together, and confirmed their responsibilities to the American People, I am announcing the formation of the Super Intelligence Force (SIF)." The order, titled "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence," established that the US government will no longer recognise or use Artificial Intelligence or AI as terminology in official settings to the maximum extent permitted by law.
Under the presidential mandate, Trump said that the SIF is designed to serve as the government's primary liaison across civil society, safety advocacy, and private industry. Trump outlined the wide scope of outreach to "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence." "The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans," he wrote.
Trump specified that the Super Intelligence Force will coordinate government engagement with "Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies." The Super Intelligence Force will be led by a four-member leadership team spanning national intelligence, defence, regulatory, and federal personnel operations. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Chief Technology Officer and Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor will direct the agency.
Trump stated that the leadership group will report directly to "the President of the United States (ME!), and the Chief of Staff, Susie Wiles". Under the executive order signed by Trump earlier this week, the administration temporarily applies the existing statutory definition of artificial intelligence under Title 15 of the United States Code to "Super Intelligence."
Additionally, the directive sets a 60-day deadline for the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST) to submit proposed legislative language to Congress to establish an updated federal statutory definition of "Super Intelligence" and recommend conforming amendments to existing US laws. Earlier, President Trump hosted a high-level luncheon at the White House with top technology executives—including SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, among others—where he framed the technological leap as an unprecedented era for humanity.
Emphasising the scale of the sector, Trump had stated: "It is the biggest thing there is — maybe the biggest thing there's ever been. It's much bigger than the Internet. This is unbelievable growth for our country — and we have all of them."Following the meeting, tech leaders and administration officials briefed reporters on a White House Accord focused on developing Super Intelligence safely. Commenting on the initiative, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said, "We want to give the American people and our customers confidence that the technology works in the way we intended."
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei underlined the need for collaborative execution, stating,  "We all need to work together to make sure that we can win and we can win safely. If we do this right, if we work with the President and everyone here, we can win safely." Highlighting the defence and intelligence dimensions of the discussions, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton noted: "The consensus today around that national security issue was being a leader in America in AI is the most important thing for national security." (ANI)

items.body:
Andrius Sytas　Terje Solsvik

[リガ ４日 ロイター] - ラトビアで３日に実施された総選挙は、親ウクライナ・中道のクルベルグス首相率いる「連合リスト」が予想を上回る大差で勝利した。開票速報で明らかになった。ロシアによる攻撃の可能性に対する警戒が高まる中、多くの有権者が緊張感を抱えながら投票に臨んだ。

開票率８８％の時点で、連合リストの得票率は３６．６％。ポピュリスト政党「ラトビア・ファースト」 が１３．４％で続いた。

バルト諸国はこの数カ月、ロシアがウクライナ支援の切り崩しと社会不安の醸成を狙って、欧州各地で破壊工作やサイバー攻撃などのハイブリッド攻撃を仕掛けていると警告してきた。ロシア側は、こうした非難には根拠がないと反発している。

クルベルグス氏は３日夕、リガにある党本部で、「驚くほどよい結果だ。ここまでとは予想していなかった」と述べ、首相続投に意欲を示した。

開票速報によれば、単独過半数には達していないため、組閣には連立が必要となる。同氏は、ラトビア・ファーストとの連立は望まないと述べた。

親ロシアの「主権」は出口調査で得票率１１．６％で３位、ロシアに対する強硬路線を掲げる右派政党「国民連合」が９．１％だった。

クルベルグス氏は選挙戦で、対ドローン能力の強化や国防費を国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比５％に維持すると約束した。この水準はＮＡＴＯ加盟国の中でも最も高い部類に入る。ラトビア・ファーストは、国内のロシア系住民の支持取り込みを図った。

親ロシア政党は、ウクライナへの支援を全てやめて、特にロシア語を話す少数派の生活費の問題にもっと力を入れるべきだと主張した。

items.title: Bosnia votes Sunday in election that could affect EU bid
items.author: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
items.creator: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
items.summary: Voters are casting ballots for the central tripartite presidency and national parliament.
items.body:
Bosnians are voting on Sunday in elections that could affect their country's European Union membership bid and the influence that the United States and Russia seek over the small Balkan nation.
Voters are casting ballots for the country's central tripartite presidency and national parliament, alongside regional legislative races in its two federal entities.
Some polling stations had to be temporarily closed due to problems with the electronic voting system, Bosnia's Central Election Commission head Jovan Kalaba told reporters in Sarajevo. The commission redesigned ballots and introduced new biometric voter identification and electronic scanners, which it said were aimed at curbing voting fraud.
In a statement later in the day, the commission said that voter turnout was 28.8% by 3 p.m. (1300 GMT), or 8.12 percentage points less than at the same time during elections in 2022.
Voter frustration has grown over an economic slowdown, the slow pace of EU entry talks and a lingering political crisis in which ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities have repeatedly stalled decisions by the weak central government that links them.
Bosnia, which has struggled to recover from the bloody 1992-95 war, secured EU candidate status in December 2022 and approval to open accession negotiations in 2024. Actual talks have not started because domestic political leaders have yet to enact core requirements such as bolstering judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption laws.
Louis Crishock, an American diplomat and the acting High Representative for Bosnia who, under the provisions of the Dayton accord, enforces the laws in Bosnia, urged people to go and vote.
"Your vote is your chance to shape the next four years. Cast freely and with confidence that your vote will be counted as cast," Crishock wrote on X after visiting some polling stations earlier in the day.
The election commission is expected to release preliminary after polls close at 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) on Sunday.
MOVING BEYOND DIVISIVE RHETORIC The Bosnian war ended in 1995 with the US-brokered Dayton peace accord, which left the country split along ethnic lines into the Serb-dominated Republika Srpska and the Bosniak-Croat Federation — linked by the central government and tripartite presidency.
Many voters in the country of 3.4 million people say they want to move beyond the divisive rhetoric, but the politics appears stuck.
The vote pits rival ethnic parties — the Bosniak SDA, Serb SNSD and Croat HDZ BiH — against multi-ethnic opposition coalitions led by the Social Democratic Party.
According to tracking platform Poliwave, the SDA holds a narrow national lead with 21.4%, followed by the SDP on 16.7%. In Republika Srpska, SNSD, the party run by secessionist leader Milorad Dodik, who wants close ties with Serbia and Russia [USN:S8N3KH02O TEXT:"and is at odds"] with the government in Sarajevo, is ahead with 34.2%.
"We are ... choosing those who can manage certain processes, build society, and make the Republika Srpska peaceful and stable," said Zeljka Cvijanovic, the SNSD candidate who is seeking a second term in the tripartite presidency.
If ethnically based parties prevail and continue their disputes within the central government, the body that would eventually officially join the EU, progress on accession is likely to stall further.
In the capital, Sarajevo, Ismar Garasljevic, a 51-year-old high school teacher, said: "More than 30 years after the war, the situation is still the same; we are talking about nationalism ... The same faces, the same story, constantly."
Major powers have long sought influence over Bosnia. The EU is seeking to expand its membership across the Balkans, including Bosnia, but Russia is slowing it down, maintaining its support of the Republika Srpska.
The US has also sought influence and wants to push for a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N40Y0SF TEXT:"pipeline project"] to import US liquefied natural gas, run by a company with links to the Trump administration, but the EU warned that the company selection lacked competitive transparency. Washington has also clashed with Brussels over the role of the international [USN:L6N41N07W TEXT:"High Representative."]

items.title: Los 8 países con mayor biodiversidad en el mundo y el tamaño de sus economías en 2026
items.author: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
items.summary: La biodiversidad de estos países representa una oportunidad para desarrollar la bioeconomía y, al mismo tiempo, una responsabilidad para preservar sus ecosistemas en medio de crecientes amenazas como ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — América Latina, Asia y Oceanía concentran algunos de los territorios con mayor biodiversidad en el mundo. Brasil encabeza el listado de países con mayor biodiversidad, medido en términos de las especies animales y vegetales del planeta que concentra su territorio. De acuerdo con cifras recogidas por el portal de estadísticas Statista, Brasil concentra casi 13% de las especies de seres vivos del planeta en una superficie terrestre de aproximadamente 8,5 millones de km². Los datos se desprenden del estudio de World Rainforests , elaborado por el escritor y activista Rhett Ayers Butler, que ha sido citado por Statista. Ver más: Los bosques más extensos de Latinoamérica y qué tan lejos están de la “deforestación cero” Fuentes como Naciones Unidas han reseñado que Brasil cuenta con más de 120.000 especies de invertebrados, cerca de 9.000 vertebrados y más de 4.000 especies de plantas. Brasil, su vez, tiene la mayor economía de Latinoamérica, con un PIB estimado en los US$2,64 billones por el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI). En el listado de los países más biodiversos del mundo le sigue Indonesia , que concentra el 10,36% de las especies con una superficie terrestre de aproximadamente 1,9 millones de km². Indonesia tiene un PIB estimado de US$1,54 billones. Luego aparece China (9,80%), con una extensión de 9,6 millones de km² y un PIB de US$20,85 billones. Colombia (9,47%) aparece cuarta en el listado de países más biodiversos del mundo. Su extensión es de 1,14 millones de km² y su PIB es de unos US$539.530 millones. Según información oficial, Colombia es líder mundial en aves, orquídeas y mariposas. Ver más: Mapa de los países de ingresos más altos y bajos en Latinoamérica, según el Banco Mundial Después de estos países figuran otros dos latinoamericanos, Perú (8,56%) y México (8,29%). En el caso de Perú, el país tiene aproximadamente 1,29 millones de km² de superficie terrestre y un PIB de US$380.900 millones. En Perú, la agencia estatal Andina reseña que el país tiene al menos 510 especies de reptiles y 490 de mamíferos. Cuenta con 19.812 especies vegetales y 1.861 especies de aves. Además, contabiliza 1.583 especies de peces y 655 de anfibios. Entre tanto, México tiene una extensión de 1,94 millones de km² y un PIB de US$2,12 billones. En México se han contabilizado unas 614 especies de mamíferos, hasta 1.150 de aves, 995 de reptiles y 428 de anfibios. Después de estos países latinoamericanos aparece en el listado Australia (8,11%), con 7,69 millones de km² de superficie terrestre. Su PIB se estima en los US$2,12 billones. Y el top 10 lo cierra la India (7,58%), con una extensión de 3,29 millones de km² y un PIB de US$4,15 billones. Statista reseña que entre los países que albergan al menos 1% de las especies animales y vegetales del mundo, Singapur ocupa el primer lugar, seguido por Brunéi, Esuatini, Ruanda y Burundi. Eslovenia, Montenegro y Bután también destacan por la diversidad de sus ecosistemas. La riqueza natural también abre oportunidades para actividades vinculadas con la economía verde, desde soluciones climáticas hasta nuevos negocios basados en recursos biológicos. Bloomberg informó a mediados de año que la economía verde, las líneas de negocio de las empresas cotizadas a nivel mundial que generan ingresos a partir de soluciones climáticas, alcanza ahora un valor de mercado récord de US$10 billones. Este aumento se produjo al elevarse los ingresos vinculados a productos y servicios medioambientales hasta los US$5,5 billones el año pasado, registrando su ritmo de crecimiento más rápido desde 2022, según un informe publicado este miércoles por London Stock Exchange Group Plc. América Latina alberga algunas de las áreas forestales más extensas y biodiversas del planeta, encabezadas por la selva Amazónica, considerado el bosque tropical más grande del mundo. Esta abarca una extensión de 6,7 millones de km2 (el doble del tamaño de la India), según cálculos del Fondo Mundial para la Naturaleza (WWF, por su sigla en inglés). A esta le siguen el Gran Chaco, el segundo bosque más grande de Sudamérica con más de 1,1 millones de km², que se extiende entre Argentina, Paraguay, Bolivia y Brasil. Se trata de una extensión que duplica “con creces” la del estado de California, según WWF. “Es una de las últimas fronteras del continente y está amenazada por el desarrollo agrícola, principalmente para la producción de carne de vacuno y soja”. Después figura la Mata Atlántica, con una extensión estimada en 1 millón de Km2, un bosque húmedo que va desde Brasil hasta el noreste de Argentina y el este de Paraguay. Asimismo, sobresalen los bosques templados valdivianos en el centro-sur de Chile y Argentina, que cubren aproximadamente entre 250.000 y 300.000 km 2 . También destaca la Selva Maya, el bosque tropical más extenso en Mesoamérica, que se extiende por 150.000 kilómetros cuadrados entre Belice, el norte de Guatemala y el sureste de México. Las principales amenazas identificadas por WWF para la Selva Maya se concentran en la degradación ambiental y el cambio de uso del suelo, impulsados primordialmente por la expansión de las actividades agropecuarias y el uso de pesticidas. A estas presiones se suman los incendios forestales, la tala ilegal y el tráfico ilícito de flora y fauna. Moskitia es considerado el segundo bosque más grande de Centroamérica, con una extensión de 22.568 km2 entre Honduras y Nicaragua. Otra de las grandes áreas forestales de la región es el Tapón del Darién, con una extensión de 5.750 km2 de selva tropical que sirve de frontera natural entre Colombia y Panamá. Además de los bosques, América Latina concentra una proporción enorme del agua dulce del planeta, tanto en grandes ríos como en humedales, glaciares y acuíferos, pero toda esta riqueza hídrica está bajo presión ante fenómenos como el cambio climático, la deforestación, la degradación de ecosistemas, la sobreexplotación, la contaminación y una débil gobernanza. La riqueza está asociada a grandes cuencas hidrográficas como la Amazonía y el Orinoco, así como a sistemas subterráneos estratégicos como el Acuífero Guaraní, que comparten Brasil, Argentina, Paraguay y Uruguay. Esta combinación de ríos, humedales, acuíferos y bosques hace que América Latina sea un pilar fundamental para la seguridad hídrica, la biodiversidad y la resiliencia climática del planeta. items.title: Des explosions entendues pendant la visite du chancelier allemand à Kyiv
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Des sirènes d'alerte aérienne et des explosions ont retenti dimanche dans la capitale ukrainienne, Kyiv, alors que le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz rendait visite au président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky dans le cadre du renouvellement du soutien de l'Allemagne à l'Ukraine.
items.body:
Des sirènes d'alerte aérienne et des explosions ont retenti dimanche dans la capitale ukrainienne, Kyiv, alors que le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz rendait visite au président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky dans le cadre du renouvellement du soutien de l'Allemagne à l'Ukraine.
Alors que la Russie intensifie son offensive contre l'Ukraine, Friedrich Merz, accompagné de dirigeants d'entreprises du secteur de la défense dans le cadre de cette visite surprise, a exhorté Moscou à mettre fin à ses attaques croissantes.
Le chancelier allemand a annoncé une aide militaire à l'Ukraine d'une valeur d'environ un milliard d'euros et un programme de soutien énergétique.
Friedrich Merz et Volodimir Zelensky ont visité le bâtiment gravement endommagé de l'Académie des sciences d'Ukraine, où au moins deux personnes sont mortes la semaine dernière lors d'une frappe de drones.
La Russie pilonne actuellement le cœur de Kyiv avec certaines des frappes de drones, l'offensive la plus importante dans la capitale depuis le début de la guerre en 2022.
"Je ne peux que le répéter une fois de plus: Monsieur Poutine, mettez fin à cette guerre insensée", a déclaré Friedrich Merz.
"Nous sommes prêts à dialoguer, nous sommes prêts à discuter de la fin de cette guerre, mais ces attaques barbares contre la population civile ukrainienne doivent cesser", a-t-il imploré.
Dimanche matin, quatre alertes aériennes ont été entendues dans la capitale ukrainienne, accompagnées d'explosions et de détonations des systèmes de défense aérienne.
L'une des frappes russes a touché le pont Nord sur le fleuve Dniepr, endommageant sa chaussée, a déclaré le maire de Kyiv, Vitali Klitschko, sur la messagerie Telegram. Il a précisé que cette frappe avait fait deux blessés et provoqué des dégâts sur le réseau d'eau chaude du secteur.
Depuis la semaine dernière, la Russie attaque les ponts de Kyiv afin de perturber les liaisons entre les deux rives de la capitale et les voies logistiques entre le centre et l'est de l'Ukraine.
Friedrich Merz a souligné que son déplacement à Kyiv "démontrait que nous ne nous laisserons pas intimider".
"Pas plus qu'une attaque de drone survenant au moment même de notre visite", a-t-il dénoncé.
Selon Volodimir Zelensky, Vladimir Poutine tente d'affaiblir la résistance ukrainienne en intensifiant les frappes aériennes contre Kyiv et d'autres villes.
"Ils s'en prennent aux ponts — pensent-ils vraiment que nous ne réagirons pas? Je suis tout simplement stupéfait par cette volonté animale d'envenimer la situation chaque jour", a-t-il déclaré lors d'une conférence de presse, aux côtés du chancelier allemand.
Avant cette déclaration, le ministère russe de la Défense a Russie, en réponse à une interview du président ukrainien dans laquelle il s'était engagé à intensifier les attaques contre les raffineries russes, avait assuré que Moscou accroîtrerait ses frappes sur Kyiv et d'autres régions d'Ukraine, notamment les installations militaires, les sites de l'industrie de la défense et les infrastructures.
DES RÉFORMES DEMANDÉES PAR L'UE Le chancelier allemand est arrivé à Kyiv accompagné de la ministre de l'Economie, Katherina Reiche, et d'une délégation comprenant des dirigeants de Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, Diehl Defence, Quantum Systems et d'autres entreprises.
Friedrich Merz devait également faire pression sur le gouvernement ukrainien pour qu'il progresse sur les réformes demandées par les partenaires de l'UE, notamment dans la lutte contre la corruption.
Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré mercredi, après s'être entretenu par téléphone avec Friedrich Merz, que l'Ukraine finaliserait prochainement un accord conclu avec l'Allemagne pour la production de drones, de missiles et des logiciels associés.
L'un des principaux axes de développement devrait être la production rapide de drones antiaériens, que la société allemande Quantum, spécialisée dans les technologies de défense, a testés avec succès.
Depuis l'été, la Russie utilise quotidiennement des dizaines de drones d'attaque à réaction à grande vitesse pour cibler des infrastructures civiles et militaires.
En avril, Quantum et le fabricant ukrainien WIY Drones ont annoncé la création de Quantum WIY Industries, une coentreprise destinée à produire le drone intercepteur Strila et les technologies de défense aérienne associées.
L'accord prévoit également le développement et la production conjoints d'armes d'une portée de plus de 1.000 km que l'Ukraine peut utiliser pour lancer des attaques en profondeur à l'intérieur de la Russie.

items.title: Merz unveils fresh military aid in Kyiv, says Germany won't be intimidated
items.author: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
items.creator: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
items.summary: Germany's chancellor said Moscow was trying to break the morale of the Ukrainian people, and announced €350 million for repairs in the energy sector.
items.body:
Germany will not be intimidated into dropping its support for Ukraine, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Sunday as he announced a further €1 billion ($1.1 billion) in military aid during a visit to Kyiv marked by Russian drone attacks.
Air-raid sirens and explosions rang out repeatedly across the Ukrainian capital as Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy visited a memorial to soldiers killed during the four-year-old war, as well as the [USN:L1N45K0A2 TEXT:"Academy of Sciences"], where at least two people died in a drone strike last week.
Russia has escalated its drone attacks on Kyiv and other cities in recent weeks, targeting telecoms, electricity and transport infrastructure as well as military assets.
Speaking at a press conference alongside Zelenskiy, Merz said Moscow was trying to break the morale of the Ukrainian people, and announced €350 million for repairs in the energy sector. He said Germany remained Ukraine's strongest backer.
DEALS WITH GERMAN COMPANIES WORTH €6.6 BILLION "We do this not only to protect Ukraine's territorial integrity; we do it deeply in our own interest, for it is a matter of Europe's security," Merz said, noting that Russia was carrying out cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns that struck at Europe's democratic order.
"This demonstrates that we will not be intimidated," he said.
Russia has said accusations of hybrid warfare are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.
German officials said executives from companies, who travelled with Merz, had signed 14 agreements with the Ukrainian government and businesses worth roughly €6.6 billion.
Among those deals, Ukraine inked an agreement with Germany's Diehl Defence for the supply of IRIS-T air defence missiles, as well as a deal for radar equipment with Hensoldt and for jet drone interceptors with Quantum Systems.
"What is important in this visit is that not only Germany is helping Ukraine, but Ukraine is sharing its knowledge, experience, as well as orders," Zelenskiy said. "These are jobs for Germany."
Zelenskiy praised a new jet drone interceptor, dubbed SPYS and developed by Quantum, for showing promising results. He said Ukraine and Germany were close to [USN:L1N44U0N8 TEXT:"finalising a broad defence deal"], which he has previously said would include the production of drones, missiles and related software.
ZELENSKIY VOWS TO RESPOND Since the summer, Russia has targeted civilian and military infrastructure daily with dozens of high-speed jet-powered [USN:L8N4521KI TEXT:"attack drones"] – which Ukraine has struggled to down because they are much faster than previous propeller versions.
One of the Russian strikes on Sunday hit the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro River, damaging its roadway, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram. The explosion injured two people and damaged a hot water supply system in the area, he said.
Zelenskiy said Russia's decision to escalate air strikes against infrastructure targets was due to setbacks it had suffered on the battlefield, and he vowed that Ukraine would retaliate. He said Russian President Vladimir Putin wanted to force residents to flee Ukraine's major cities.
"If our bridges collapse, we will manage to get out of this situation, but his people will feel it too ... This is maximum escalation of this war," Zelenskiy told reporters.
Russia has been [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"attacking"] Kyiv's bridges since last week in an effort to disrupt links between the capital's two sides and logistics routes between central and eastern Ukraine.
MERZ APPEALS FOR END TO 'SENSELESS WAR' Zelenskiy said US peace envoy Steve Witkoff has messaged him to urge a return to trilateral talks as soon as possible. He said Ukraine was willing to meet this month and hoped Russia would join, but he said Western allies needed to apply more pressure to Moscow to bring the war to an end.
Earlier in the day, during the visit to the badly damaged Academy of Sciences, Merz appealed to Putin to "put an end to this senseless war".
"We are ready for talks, we are ready to discuss bringing this war to an end, but these barbaric attacks on the civilian population of Ukraine must stop," the German leader said.
Russia's Foreign Ministry [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"said"] on Saturday that Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in Ukraine in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia. It warned foreign nationals and diplomatic staff against travelling to Ukraine.
($1 = 0.8887 euros)

items.title: “I don’t go to sets with a phone": Paul Rudd reveals his new habit during movie shoots
items.summary: Actor Paul Rudd revealed that he doesn't take his phone on the sets of the film because he is addicted to it, Variety reported.
items.body:
“I don’t go to sets with a phone": Paul Rudd reveals his new habit during movie shoots  Actor Paul Rudd revealed that he doesn't take his phone on the sets of the film because he is addicted to it, Variety reported. 
ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 17:23 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 17:23 IST

Paul Rudd (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Actor Paul Rudd revealed that he doesn't take his phone on the sets of the film because he is addicted to it, Variety reported. The actor is set to play the moderator of the first-ever meeting dedicated to solving America’s climate crisis in “A Statement,” the latest film from Oscar-winning director Tom McCarthy.
Set at a Florida beachside resort in 1980, the film follows 20 experts who spend a weekend in a conference room and figure out their differences over how to draft a statement to Congress about the effects of carbon dioxide emissions on the climate, reported Variety. The cast includes Paul Giamatti, Tatiana Maslany and John Turturro and the actor admitted that he feels more connected to the ensemble cast by leaving his smartphone in his trailer, a practice he claims he’s now followed for some time.
“I don’t go to sets with a phone. I haven’t done that for a while now. It’s important to put it down. Anytime. They’re horrible things. I’m addicted to it like everybody else. They’re facilitating our own destruction,” he told Variety Saturday evening during the film’s world premiere at the New York Film Festival. Rudd revealed that director McCarthy enforced a “very strict no phones policy” on the set of “A Statement,” which he found brought his castmates closer together and made filming feel more like a play.
“The world has changed since cell phones have existed. We don’t look at each other or talk to each other quite the same way. Now, [with the phone ban], we were forced to really spend time with each other and talk. Working on a movie set in 1980, we’re dressed in a certain kind of way. It felt like, ‘Oh, yeah. I remember this. This feels like it used to feel when people sat around and spoke to one another,’” added Paul Rudd, as quoted by Variety. (ANI)

items.title: テニス＝世界ランク1位シナー、マスターズ上海大会欠場を発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスの世界ランキング１位、ヤニク・シナー（２５、イタリア）は３日、長引いている膝のけがの影響で、マスターズ上海大会（７日開幕）を欠場すると発表した。

シナーは７月１２日にウィンブルドン選手権決勝でアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）を下して以来、公式戦でプレーしていない。２０２４年のマスターズ上海大会では、決勝でノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）を下し、優勝した。

シナーはインスタグラムのストーリーズに「残念ながら今年はマスターズ上海大会でプレーできない。上海のファンの前でプレーするのは楽しいだけに、来週プレーできないことを申し訳なく思う」とつづり、「来年会えることを楽しみにしています」と締めくくった。

シナーの今年の成績は４４勝３敗。ウィンブルドンで四大大会５回目の優勝を達成した。

今年のマスターズ上海大会にはディフェンディングチャンピオンのバレンティン・バチェロット（モナコ）、同大会４回優勝のジョコビッチ、世界ランク２位のズベレフ、同３位のカルロス・アルカラス（スペイン）らが出場する。

items.title: ゴルフ＝ロッテ選手権で山下が6位浮上、ティティクル単独首位
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのロッテ選手権は３日、米ハワイ州エワビーチのホアカレイＣＣ（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、山下美夢有が６位に順位を上げた。

７位でスタートした山下は６バーディー、１ダブルボギー、１ボギーの３アンダー６９でラウンド。通算１２アンダーの２０４とした。同じく７位で出た畑岡奈紗は２アンダー７０で回ったが、通算１１アンダーの９位に後退した。

岩井千怜と笹生優花はともに４アンダーで回り、通算９アンダーの１８位に浮上した。吉田優利と竹田麗央は通算８アンダーの２４位。西郷真央は通算７アンダーの３０位。西村優菜は４２位、櫻井心那は５３位、岩井明愛は６５位となった。

通算１７アンダーに伸ばしたジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）が単独首位。ユン・イナ（韓国）とポリー・マック（ドイツ）が３打差の２位で並んでいる。

items.title: Japan's Takaichi protests to US after Marine accused of murder in Okinawa
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
items.body:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered a protest with the United States on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Okinawa.
Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday and taking her wallet and backpack, police said. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and vicious incident is extremely regrettable," Takaichi said in a statement.
"The government of Japan strongly protests to the US side and strongly seeks maximum cooperation with the investigation," as well as the tightening of discipline and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence, she said.
Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, in comments carried by national broadcaster NHK, said: "Such an incident is unacceptable and I am deeply outraged."
The US embassy and the Marine Corps expressed condolences over the incident and said they were cooperating with the Japanese authorities.
The Marines said in a statement that the suspect, who is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force and based at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was in Japanese custody.
"The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behaviour," it said.
Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972. Their presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.
The 1995 rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen sparked mass protests.
Saturday's killing could complicate Takaichi's efforts to [USN:L1N455098 TEXT:"relocate some Marines"] from the busy Futenma air base to a more remote facility at Henoko. Opponents want the troops moved out of the prefecture.
Okinawa, which is 100 km (60 miles) from Taiwan at the closest point, is viewed by Tokyo and Washington as key in deterring potential military aggression from China.
