items.title: テニス＝ルバキナ、世界ランク1位としての初戦で逆転負け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - テニスの中国オープン（ＯＰ）は３日、北京で試合を行い、女子シングルス２回戦で世界ランキング１位のエレーナ・ルバキナ（カザフスタン）が初戦敗退を喫した。

この日が初戦となった第１シードのルバキナは、アリーナ・チャラエワ（アルメニア）と対戦し、第１セットは６─３で奪ったものの、続くセットを４─６、３─６で落として逆転負け。９月の全米ＯＰで優勝し、キャリア初の世界ランク１位となったルバキナだが、トップに浮上した後の最初の試合で敗れた選手としては、大坂なおみに次ぐ史上２人目となった。

ＷＴＡランキングは１９７５年に初めて発表されたが、ＯｐｔａＡｃｅによると、それ以降で世界ランク１位の相手に逆転勝ちを収めた選手では、今回のチャラエワ（１１８位）が最もランクの低いプレーヤーだという。

ルバキナは「間違いなく、今日は非常に厳しい試合だった。全米ＯＰで優勝してからいろいろなことがあった。睡眠や回復の機会をあまり持てなかった。アリーナをお祝いしたい。彼女は素晴らしい試合をした」と話した。

items.title: La saga de la deuda de Paramount concluye con un final escalofriante
items.author: Claire Ruckin
items.summary: Si la búsqueda de financiamiento para la audaz adquisición de Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. por parte de Paramount Skydance Corp., de David Ellison, fuera una serie dramática de prestigio, los últimos d ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Un elenco de miles de personas. Récords batidos. Pérdidas inmediatas y llamadas telefónicas airadas. Si la búsqueda, que se prolongó durante meses, de financiación para la audaz adquisición de Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. por parte de Paramount Skydance Corp., de David Ellison, fuera una serie dramática de prestigio, los últimos días habrían sido el caótico final de temporada. En tan solo una semana, Paramount vendió US$52.000 millones en préstamos y bonos en distintos mercados y continentes —un plazo muy ajustado para cualquier operación de deuda destinada a financiar una adquisición, y más aún para una de las mayores financiaciones de los últimos tiempos—. Esto allana el camino para que Ellison cierre la adquisición de Warner por valor de US$110.000 millones de dólares y obtenga el control de su catálogo de películas, así como de sus negocios de streaming y videojuegos, antes del 6 de octubre, tras meses de retrasos. Ver más: Paramount cambiará su nombre a Skydance cuando se concrete la compra de Warner Bros. Sin embargo, los costes de los intereses de Paramount son ahora mucho más elevados de lo que habrían sido si hubiera emitido deuda tan solo unos meses antes, después de que las preocupaciones por la inflación elevaran los costes de financiación a nivel mundial. Además, la caída inmediata del valor de la deuda en los mercados provocó quejas por parte de los inversores, que se vieron atrapados con cuantiosas pérdidas contables en sus nuevas participaciones. Los costes adicionales por intereses —estimados entre US$250 y US$500 millones al año— también podrían dificultar la gestión de la empresa fusionada. La empresa ya tiene previsto recortar unos ambiciosos US$6.000 millones al año en gastos para mantener el apalancamiento bajo control. Las acciones de Paramount se hundieron casi un 10% el jueves, cuando se cerró el acuerdo de deuda, y apenas registraron variaciones durante la sesión bursátil de mediodía del día siguiente en Nueva York. Dennis Cinelli, director financiero de Paramount, afirmó que la fusión era una “inversión estratégica a largo plazo en la reestructuración del sector de los medios de comunicación, y los inversores la están valorando desde ese punto de vista”. El antiguo ejecutivo de Uber Technologies Inc. estableció una comparación con la accidentada oferta pública inicial que marcó el debut de la empresa de transporte compartido como sociedad cotizada. “En un mercado volátil” para la deuda, señaló Cinelli en una entrevista, “estamos satisfechos con el resultado obtenido”. Este relato de la maratón de Paramount en el mercado de deuda —y, posteriormente, del sprint hacia la línea de meta— se basa en conversaciones con varias personas con conocimiento del acuerdo, quienes solicitaron no ser identificadas al tratar información privada. El proceso comenzó en febrero, cuando Paramount se impuso a Netflix Inc. en una reñida guerra de ofertas por Warner. Bank of America Corp. y Citigroup Inc., en colaboración con Apollo Global Management Inc., concedieron un préstamo a corto plazo de US$57.500 millones, en una de las mayores operaciones de financiación puente de la historia. Posteriormente, los dos bancos vendieron parte de la deuda a otras entidades para reducir su propio riesgo. Desde el principio, la empresa y sus banqueros dejaron claro que emitirían tanto bonos de alta calificación como bonos de alto riesgo para refinanciar la operación. Esa estrategia inusual complicó la operación, pero ofreció a Paramount acceso a múltiples mercados para recaudar las inmensas sumas que necesitaba. Citigroup y Bank of America realizaron un sondeo entre los posibles compradores. A partir de junio, recogieron órdenes informales, lo que contribuyó a garantizar que el dinero estuviera disponible cuando la operación se lanzara finalmente. La demanda fue fuerte, según algunas de las personas consultadas, pero la exhaustiva preparación indicaba que a algunos banqueros les preocupaba que el entusiasmo pudiera no durar. Los bancos también temían verse atrapados como en 2022, cuando los mercados se paralizaron y les dejaron con pérdidas por valor de miles de millones de dólares en préstamos “atascados” sin vender. A algunos inversores les preocupaba el historial decepcionante de las fusiones en el sector de los medios de comunicación, muy endeudadas, incluidas aquellas en las que participaba Warner. En parte para ganarse la confianza de las agencias de calificación crediticia, Ellison, director ejecutivo de Paramount, había prometido en privado que tanto él como su empresa se comprometían a reducir el apalancamiento de Paramount, y S&P Global Ratings afirmó que se había comprometido a utilizar el patrimonio familiar si fuera necesario. En julio, todas las piezas estaban en su sitio para un posible megacontrato de deuda, pero las demandas presentadas por los fiscales generales de varios estados de EE.UU. y por un sindicato de guionistas retrasaron la fusión. Esto frustró a algunos banqueros, ya que los préstamos puente amenazaban con limitar su capacidad para financiar nuevas fusiones y adquisiciones. Entonces se produjo un repunte inesperado de los rendimientos de los bonos del Estado y un aumento de los diferenciales de crédito. Los bancos se vieron en cierta medida protegidos; a diferencia de muchas financiaciones de adquisiciones con calificación de alto riesgo, los bonos y los préstamos se habían estructurado de tal forma que, si los costes de financiación aumentaban, sería Paramount quien corriera con el riesgo, y no ellos. No obstante, les preocupaba que las condiciones menos favorables dificultaran la venta de la operación. El avance decisivo se produjo el 21 de septiembre, cuando Paramount anunció que había llegado a un acuerdo en las demandas. Aún quedaban algunos obstáculos por superar, sobre todo que SoftBank Group Corp. estaba llevando a cabo su propia emisión récord de bonos de alto riesgo por valor de US$11.100 millones de dólares, con la ayuda de bancos como Citi. No se consideraba que el mercado de alto rendimiento, que ya se encontraba bajo cierta presión, tuviera suficiente profundidad para gestionar ambas operaciones a la vez. La financiación de SoftBank se cerró el 23 de septiembre, lo que allanó el camino para que Paramount iniciara la carrera hacia la meta un día después. Había un gran incentivo adicional: Paramount había acordado previamente pagar penalizaciones por demora de US$7 millones al día si la adquisición no se cerraba antes del 30 de septiembre. Los banqueros ya habían mantenido conversaciones telefónicas entre EE. UU. y Europa para trazar un plan de reducción de carteras, mientras que los comerciales habían llamado a los clientes para comprobar si las órdenes anteriores seguían vigentes. Los meses de preparación parecieron dar sus frutos, ya que unos 1.000 inversores realizaron pedidos de la deuda, según indicaron algunas de las personas consultadas. Muchos de los compradores eran gestores de carteras de fondos de cobertura multistrategia. Durante el proceso, se reajustó la composición de la deuda para reducir los bonos y aumentar los préstamos, respectivamente. Paramount también redujo los costes de financiación en 0,375 puntos porcentuales, o 37,5 puntos básicos, durante el proceso de venta, lo que supuso un ahorro de unos US$200 millones en intereses al año, según afirmó Cinelli, director financiero de la empresa. Si bien esto benefició a las finanzas de Paramount, el cambio provocó que algunos inversores se retiraran en el último momento, lo que supuso que aquellos que se mantuvieron en la operación se vieran cargados con más deuda de la que esperaban. Se produjeron llamadas y mensajes airados de los operadores a los suscriptores en relación con la deserción, mayor de lo habitual, en la cartera de órdenes, a medida que se desplomaban las cotizaciones de la deuda recién emitida. En un momento dado del jueves, sus pérdidas contables ascendieron a cientos de millones de dólares, pero la presión vendedora comenzó a remitir tras la oleada inicial. Una vez finalizado el proceso, la empresa y sus banqueros consideraron la venta y su rápida recuperación como un éxito indiscutible para Paramount y sus perspectivas a largo plazo: “la mayor emisión de deuda de una sola empresa de la historia”, afirmó Leon Kalvaria, presidente del grupo de clientes institucionales de Citigroup, en una entrevista. Bank of America no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios, Warner remitió la cuestión a Paramount y Apollo se negó a hacer declaraciones. Paramount aún tendrá que hacer frente a la actitud escéptica de analistas como el equipo de CreditSights, que señaló los riesgos relacionados con la gestión de la carga de deuda de esta gigantesca empresa de medios de comunicación y con el cumplimiento de los objetivos de recorte de costes y sinergias. A pesar de todo ello, también se comprometió a estrenar 30 películas al año en los estudios fusionados. “Desde una perspectiva general, se trata de un enorme voto de confianza de los mercados de deuda hacia la adquisición de Paramount”, afirmó Kalvaria. --Con la colaboración de Helene Durand, Gerson Freitas Jr. y Brian Smith. items.title: ＮＢＡ＝ピストンズ、デューレンとの契約延長を正式に発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のピストンズが３日、制限付きフリーエージェント（ＦＡ）のセンター、ジェイレン・デューレン（２２）との契約延長を正式に発表した。

これまで米スポーツ専門チャンネルＥＳＰＮとジ・アスレチックは５年総額２億ドル（約３１６億円）と報じていたが、チームは契約の詳細を明かしていない。

ピストンズのバスケットボール運営部門代表を務めるトラジャン・ラングドン氏は「今後何年もジェイレンをチームの中心に据えられることをうれしく思う」とし、「彼は若くして多くを成し遂げており、われわれは彼の全盛期はこれからだと信じている」と述べた。

報道によると、ピストンズは最近デューレンに同じ総額２億ドルの契約を提示したものの、体重に関する条項を盛り込んでいたという。今回の合意では同条項が削除されたと報じられている。

昨季初めてオールスターとオールＮＢＡに選出されたデューレンは、レギュラーシーズンで自己最多の１試合平均１９．５得点に加え、１０．５リバウンドを記録。ピストンズは６０勝２２敗で東カンファレンス最高成績を残した。一方、プレーオフでは同１０．２得点、８．５リバウンドに数字を落とし、チームは東カンファレンス準決勝でキャバリアーズに３勝４敗で敗れた。

items.summary: By Ben Makori SHERFIELD ON LODDON, England, Oct 4 (Reuters) - F lydubai's flight FZ1073, which plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, would have felt ...
items.body:
Like a 'vertical roller coaster': Simulating flight FZ1073's sudden plunge
Reuters | Updated: 04-10-2026 15:26 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 15:26 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

By Ben Makori SHERFIELD ON LODDON, England, Oct 4 (Reuters) - F lydubai's flight FZ1073, which plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, would have felt like a "vertical roller coaster", according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.
The steep fall, after an attack on the captain by the co-pilot during a flight on Wednesday, would have put huge strain on the Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft - as well as the passengers and crew, said Alberto Paduanelli, owner of ALPA Simulation in Sherfield on Loddon, southern England. The co-pilot of the flydubai jet, which was bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "terrorist attack".
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, two sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity. Reuters could not independently reach al-Hammami for comment. Flydubai says the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation and it cannot comment further. Oman has yet to comment on the incident.
"A plunge of 16,000 feet (4,877 metres) over 30 seconds will feel like you are over on a very, very vertical roller coaster," Paduanelli said, sitting at the controls of the simulator cockpit. "The difference is that on the roller coaster, you know what's happening," he said, adding that with a sudden drop "you feel the negative g-force on your body".
For passengers who are not strapped in, "Your body will literally lift from the seat", he said. Using a simulator to recreate the incident, Paduanelli said the aircraft's autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing the jet to accelerate rapidly.
US President Donald Trump has praised the Boeing jet for withstanding the severe forces put on it during the incident. The plane was levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, before a reserve crew of pilots onboard landed the plane. "It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural planning and design," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that the 737 Max "was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do".
Boeing did not respond to a request for comment. Aircraft are designed and tested to withstand substantial aerodynamic loads, but Paduanelli said a prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe.
"This was nothing but a miracle that nothing was hurt apart from the captain, unfortunately, and that two pilots were onboard," Paduanelli said. Details about al-Hammami's past have trickled out.
Royal Air Maroc told Reuters he did a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. Buckinghamshire New University in Britain said he did a distance-learning course in aviation management with the institution, but no pilot training. An Australian Federal Police spokesperson said on Sunday that authorities there were investigating al-Hammami's "links to Australia". A source briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［コルカタ（インド）　３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［コルカタ（インド）　３日　ロイター］ - サッカーの国際親善試合が３日、各地で行われ、サムエウ・リノが代表初ゴールを決めたブラジルがアウェーでインドに４─０と快勝を収めた。

ブラジルは前半２８分、右サイドから切れ込んだエステバンがネットを揺らして先制し、さらに同４２分にはペドロのゴールもアシスト。後半１３分にリノが代表初得点を挙げると、試合終盤にリノが相手の守備をかわして自身この日２点目を記録した。

世界ランキング１３８位のインドは６戦連続で未勝利に。カルロ・アンチェロッティ監督率いるブラジルはオーストラリア戦も含めた遠征を２勝１分けとした。

items.title: Cornell president vows 'serious look' at fraternities, sororities in wake of rape allegations
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Michael Kotlikoff said the school would take steps to prevent a similar situation in the future.
items.body:
Cornell University will examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following an outcry over the school's handling of a student's rape allegations, the Ivy League school's president said on Saturday.
A [USN:L1N45O0OO TEXT:"civil lawsuit"] filed last month by the woman, who alleges she was drugged and raped in 2024 by several members of the Chi Phi fraternity, has sparked [USN:L6N45O0CP TEXT:"outrage and soul-searching"] at Cornell over its campus culture at the school in Ithaca, New York.
In a video message, Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said the school would take steps to prevent a similar situation in the future. That includes "a serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life," Kotlikoff said.
"At their best, these organizations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a powerful sense of community," he said. "But being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."
The university will seek input, he said, from students, alumni and others on how to "preserve what is valuable about Greek life while strengthening individual accountability, transparency and a culture in which every member understands their responsibility to protect the safety and well-being of others."
The lawsuit against Cornell, seven fraternity members and others, alleges that the school failed to adequately punish some of the accused students.
The accused men have denied all wrongdoing, the New York Times reported.
Cornell has defended its handling of the matter, saying it launched a comprehensive investigation and barred the Chi Phi fraternity from campus. The school said it imposed a range of disciplinary measures, including expulsions.
But "we must do better," Kotlikoff said. "We don’t have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves."
He vowed that university officials would "be more transparent" about their actions related to the 2024 incident, but he did not detail specific initiatives that the university would take.
"In the coming weeks, we will create additional opportunities for members of our community to ask questions and hear directly from university leadership," he said.
The case has reignited scrutiny of how law enforcement and universities handle sexual assault complaints, with students questioning whether processes are enough to protect them. It has also drawn the attention of New York state officials, who have appointed a special prosecutor to investigate.

items.title: Ｆ１＝バーレーンＧＰ予選、フェルスタッペンが今季初ＰＰ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の第１６戦、バーレーン・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は３日、マレーシアのセパンで予選を行い、個人総合優勝４回を誇るマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ、レッドブル）が今季自身初のポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。

フェルスタッペンは１分３５秒１３０をマーク。２番手のルイス・ハミルトン（英国、フェラーリ）を０秒２９８上回った。フェルスタッペンの同僚、アイザック・ハジャー（フランス）が３番手に入ったが、パワーユニットのコンポーネント交換で、決勝では５グリッド降格のペナルティーを受ける。

総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）は４番手でシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ、フェラーリ）が５番手。ランド・ノリス（英国）が６番手、オスカー・ピアストリ（オーストラリア）が７番手とマクラーレン勢が続き、総合２位のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）は８番手に終わった。

中東情勢を受けて、今大会はマレーシアで開催されている。

items.title: イエメン軍、首都サヌアでフーシ派に空爆実施
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [４日 ロイター] - イエメン軍は４日未明、首都サヌアと北西部サアダで、親イラン武装組織フーシ派
items.body:
[４日 ロイター] - イエメン軍は４日未明、首都サヌアと北西部サアダで、親イラン武装組織フーシ派 に対して攻撃を実施していると明らかにした

軍の報道官によると、同軍は「重要目標」と称する標的を攻撃したが、詳細には触れなかった。

フーシ派系のアルマシラＴＶはこれに先立ち、サウジアラビアによるサヌアへの攻撃があったと伝えた。サウジ側からの確認は直ちには得られていない。

イランが支援するフーシ派とサウジが支援する政府軍との紛争は、２０２２年の停戦後ほぼ沈静化していたが、イラン戦争の余波で戦闘が再燃している。

フーシ派は７月にサウジに対する海上封鎖を宣言し、サウジ領土や船舶への攻撃を開始。また、イエメンの紅海沿岸で大幅に勢力域を拡大した。サウジはイエメン政府軍を支援し、同国内のフーシ派拠点に空爆を実施している。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ヤンキース主将ジャッジ、地区シリーズはロースター外
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ヤンキースが３日、レイズとの地区シリーズ（５回戦制）の２６人のロースターを発表。主将アーロン・ジャッジ外野手（３４）はメンバーを外れた。

ジャッジは右ふくらはぎの肉離れの影響で９月１６日以降プレーしておらず、その３日後に負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）入り。通算３回のア・リーグＭＶＰ（最優秀選手）選出を誇る同選手は、レッドソックスとのワイルドカードシリーズも欠場した。ヤンキースは同シリーズで２連勝し、地区シリーズに勝ち上がった。

ヤンキースのアーロン・ブーン監督は、ジャッジをロースターに入れなかったことについて「最終的にそれが最善と判断した」とコメント。「彼が復帰に近付いているように感じている」としながらも、「アーロンが本来の状態で復帰し、われわれがワールドシリーズで優勝するためには、あと１週間、彼が復帰に向けて努力を続けることが重要だ」と話した。

さらに同監督は「彼はランニングを始めたばかりで、打撃練習は数日前に再開した。これをさらに数日続けて、持久力を身に付けることが大事」とも述べた。

ジャッジは肋骨の骨折で３カ月以上離脱。９月８日に復帰した後、７試合に出場したが、打率１割７分４厘、１本塁打、３打点とふるわなかった。レギュラーシーズンでは６６試合に出場し、打率２割４分１厘、１８本塁打、４１打点だった。

items.title: サッカー＝欧州ＮＬ、イングランド7得点で大勝　スペイン3連勝
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）は３日、各地で１次リーグの試合を行い、リーグＡの３組ではイングランドが主将のハリー・ケーンらのゴールでクロアチアに７─０と大勝した。

イングランドは前半８分、ジュード・ベリンガムのパスを受けたケーンが守備陣２枚の間を抜けて先制ゴール。同２１分にベリンガムが決めて加点すると、３─０として迎えた同４５分にベリンガムのクロスからブカヨ・サカがネットを揺らした。

イングランドは後半もケーンとサカのゴールでリードを広げると、同４２分にベリンガムのお膳立てからモーガン・ロジャースにも得点が生まれた。ベリンガムは１試合１ゴール３アシスト。代表通算ゴール数を８９としたケーンは、これが１２４試合目。ピーター・シルトン氏の同代表最多出場記録まであと１試合となった。

同組のスペインはチェコを３─１で破り、開幕から３戦全勝とした。前半６分にラミン・ヤマルがペナルティーエリアの端から左足で強烈なシュートを放つと、同３５分には代表で２年以上ゴールのなかったロドリが決めて２点を先行。後半に１点を失ったが、最後はミケル・メリノのゴールで突き放した。

これにより、同組ではスペインが勝ち点９で首位、イングランドは同６で２位としている。

リーグＢの１組ではスイスがスロベニアを２─１で下して３戦全勝で首位をキープ。スコットランドは北マケドニアを２─０で破り、スロベニアと同じ勝ち点４とした。

items.title: アジア大会＝日本選手団、金メダル83個で60年ぶりに最多更新
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］　 - 愛知・名古屋アジア大会では３日、日本選手団の金メダル数が８３個に到達。これまでの記録を上回り、最多となった。１９６６年バンコク大会で記録した７８を６０年ぶりに更新した。

日本はソフトボール決勝では中国に７─０で快勝し、７連覇を達成。柔道混合団体ではカザフスタンを４─０で下し、３連覇を果たした。ラグビー７人制女子決勝では中国に１０─５で勝利し、８年ぶりの金メダル。水球男子でも優勝した。

セパタクロー男子クワッド（４人制）では日本初の金メダルに輝き、ブレイキン男子では半井重幸（ダンサー名・SHIGEKIX）が２連覇を達成。初採用のパデル、女子ダブルスは塚本早紀、徳本佳恵組が制した。

テニスの混合ダブルスでは柴原瑛菜、フレンド原ジェイ組が青山修子、楠原悠介組をストレートで下して優勝。同大会のテニス競技の決勝が日本人対決となったのは今回が初めてだった。

サッカー男子決勝では日本が韓国に０─１で敗戦。バレーボール男子決勝で、日本はイランにセットカウント１─３で負けた。

日本は今大会、３日の競技を終えた時点で銀メダルは９５個で銅メダルは９１個。金メダルと合わせて２６９個と、３４１個の中国に次ぐ２位のメダル数を記録している。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝地区シリーズ開幕、村上が先制2ラン　ドジャース大谷1安打
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［クリーブランド　３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［クリーブランド　３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のプレーオフ、地区シリーズ（５回戦制）が３日、各地で開幕。ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手はガーディアンズ戦に「４番・一塁」で出場し、四回にポストシーズン初本塁打となる先制２ランを放った。

ライトスタンドに約１３４メートルの一発をたたき込んだ村上は試合後、通訳を介し「準備はできていた。シーズンを通じてこの瞬間に向けて備えてきた」とコメントした。村上は４打数２安打２打点と活躍。ホワイトソックスは３─０でシリーズ初戦を制した。

ドジャースの大谷翔平選手はブレーブス戦に「２番・指名打者」で出場し、４打数１安打。ドジャースは５─３で勝った。先発のタリク・スクバル投手が６回１失点の好投で勝利投手となった。

items.title: Trump names intelligence chief Clayton as AI czar, to head task force
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton the administration's AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government's efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence [USN:L1N4400P3 TEXT:"Jay Clayton"] the administration's AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government's efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.
Trump, who has pushed to rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," said Clayton would head the newly created Super Intelligence Force (SIF), overseeing the government's engagement with consumers, religious groups, AI companies and other stakeholders.
In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump wrote that SIF would aim to "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence" and to "protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans."
The announcement confirmed a Wall Street Journal report in which Clayton, appointed intelligence chief in August, said Trump had tapped him to lead the administration's push to keep the US at the forefront of AI. "The risk of not being first is high," Clayton told the newspaper.
Clayton said the task force would have 120 days to produce a report assessing the risks and opportunities posed by AI and recommending what role the federal government should play.
The safety of AI has become a major issue in recent weeks, with some researchers warning that people building the technology believe it could [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"kill humans within a decade."] Several Democratic and Republican lawmakers have responded with alarm and calls for more action.
Trump has appeared to take a [USN:FWN45G0T8 TEXT:"light touch"] toward AI regulation, arguing that excessive oversight could weaken competitiveness against China. He said on Tuesday that he [USN:RTV7Cd7Qt TEXT:"does not want to work"] with Chinese President Xi Jinping on governing AI technology.
Clayton's panel will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms for breaches, hacks and other incidents, and recommend ways to strengthen federal-response capabilities under existing authorities, the Journal said, citing the task force's charter.
This is the second time Trump has named an adviser to oversee AI-related decisions across the administration. Venture capitalist David Sacks held the AI czar role at the beginning of Trump's second term.
In addition to Clayton, the task force's leaders will include Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor, Trump wrote.
The panel will report to the president and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, he said.

Oct 3 : The White House has created a task force to examine AI's risks and opportunities and recommend what role the federal government should play in overseeing the technology, with a report due within 120 days, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing the head of the task force, Jay Clayton.
Clayton, who heads the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, said he would lead the group, known as the "Super Intelligence Force," effectively serving as US President Donald Trump's AI czar, the report said, citing a senior White House official.

items.title: 北朝鮮、3日に中距離ミサイル発射　極超音速兵器の部隊訓練と国営通信
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ソウル ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ソウル ４日 ロイター] - 北朝鮮は４日、金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の立ち会いの下で３日に極超音速ミサイルの発射実験を行ったと発表した。核抑止力の信頼性を示すことを目的とした訓練だとした。国営朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が伝えた。

ミサイル発射については、金総書記の妹で朝鮮労働党の金与正総務部長が３日に公表していた。ＫＣＮＡが４日に発射に関する詳細を明らかにした。

ＫＣＮＡによると、ミサイルは極超音速戦略兵器システムの一部をなす中距離戦略ミサイルで、東部から発射され、約１０００キロ離れた日本海上の目標に命中した。ミサイル部隊を訓練するとともに、抑止戦力の効率性と機動性を評価するのが目的とした。

金総書記は、こうした活動は抑止力行使の一形態だとし、戦略攻撃兵器の「信頼性と致命性」を敵に認識させる努力を続けなければならないと述べた。核戦争抑止力の開発は国家の安全保障に不不可欠で、この方針に変わりはないと改めて表明したという。

日韓の防衛当局は３日、北朝鮮が弾道ミサイルを発射したと発表した。韓国はミサイルの飛行距離を７００キロ程度、日本は６８０キロ程度と分析している。

＜日韓のミサイル追跡能力に言及＞

金与正氏は３日、韓国と日本がミサイルを追跡できなかったと主張。変則的に飛行する「波状軌道」を採用したことで、両国の追跡能力の限界が露呈したとした。

これに対し、韓国国防省は４日、発射の準備を韓国軍が綿密に監視していたとし、発射直後にミサイルを探知・追跡し、発射地点も正確に特定したと説明した。その上で、北朝鮮が最近発射したミサイルは、韓国と米国のミサイル防衛資産で探知・迎撃できる能力の範囲内にあると評価しているとした。

ＫＣＮＡは今回、正確な着弾座標を含め、異例なほど詳しい情報を公開した。

韓国統一研究院のホン・ミン上級研究員は、こうした情報公開は、ミサイルが約１０００キロ飛行したとの主張を裏付けるとともに、北朝鮮が指摘する、韓国と日本の追跡能力の弱点を浮き彫りにすることが狙いとみている。

ホン氏によると、ミサイルは２０２２年に初めて発射実験が行われた円錐形の極超音速システムとみられる。北朝鮮が実験段階から実戦配備への移行を示唆している可能性があるという。

北朝鮮が弾道ミサイルを発射したのは９月２０日以来。今回は、非武装地帯（ＤＭＺ）で発生した地雷の爆発を巡って韓国と非難の応酬を続ける中で実施した。

韓国は、北朝鮮の地雷で自国の兵士が重傷を負ったと主張。与正氏は２日、韓国側の非難を「根拠がない」として一蹴し、韓国側の謝罪要求も退けている。

items.title: ウクライナ、ロシア製油所攻撃を強化へ　「新ドクトリンに対抗」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Daniel Flynn　Olena Harmash

［キーウ　３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Daniel Flynn　Olena Harmash

［キーウ　３日　ロイター］ - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、ロシアがキーウなどの都市から住民を退去させることを狙った新たな空爆方針を打ち出したとして、対抗措置としてロシアの製油所への攻撃を強化すると述べた。ただ、民間人は標的にしないと強調した。ロイターのインタビューで語った。

ゼレンスキー氏によると、ウクライナの情報機関は、ロシアのプーチン大統領が冬を前に、これまでよりはるかに広範な民間施設への軍事攻撃を認める「新たなドクトリン」を示した文書を入手した。

ゼレンスキー氏は「われわれは文書を確認しており、インフラや物流施設、特に都市や村、あらゆる場所の道路、学校、病院への攻撃を認めていることを把握している」と説明。「首都や各地の都市から立ち去るよう住民に圧力をかける。これが作戦の目的だ」と述べた。

背景には、前線の重要地域でロシア軍が支配地を失い、死傷者も増える中、プーチン氏が強さを誇示したいと考えていることがあると指摘した。

ロシア大統領府のコメントは得られていない。一方、ロシア外務省は、外国人にキーウからの退去を促す声明で、ここ数カ月のウクライナによる対ロシア攻撃への報復として、今後も組織的な攻撃を続けると表明した。

items.title: LE POINT sur les élections au Brésil
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Quelque 160 millions d'électeurs brésiliens sont appelés aux urnes dimanche à l'occasion du premier tour de l'élection présidentielle, un scrutin décisif pour le plus grand pays d'Amérique du Sud qui déterminera s'il emprunte à son tour le virage ultra-conservateur observé sur le continent.
items.body:
Quelque 160 millions d'électeurs brésiliens sont appelés aux urnes dimanche à l'occasion du premier tour de l'élection présidentielle, un scrutin décisif pour le plus grand pays d'Amérique du Sud qui déterminera s'il emprunte à son tour le virage ultra-conservateur observé sur le continent.
Selon les sondages, le président sortant de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui brigue à 80 ans un quatrième mandat non consécutif, est au coude-à-coude avec le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro, 45 ans, fils de l'ex-président Jair Bolsonaro condamné à 27 ans de prison pour tentative de coup d'Etat.
Treize candidats au total sont en lice pour accéder au palais du Planalto, dans un scrutin où le vote est obligatoire pour les Brésiliens âgés de 18 à 70 ans. Un second tour sera organisé le 25 octobre si aucun candidat n'emporte la majorité absolue dimanche.
Outre l'élection présidentielle se tiennent également les 4 et 25 octobre les élections parlementaires visant à renouveler les 513 sièges de la Chambre des députés et un tiers des 81 sièges du Sénat composant le Congrès national.
Les électeurs doivent également désigner les gouverneurs des 26 États fédérés et renouveler les assemblées législatives de ces derniers.
Voici les principaux développements et éléments à savoir:
* Les Brésiliens se rendent aux urnes dans un contexte de forte polarisation [USN:L6N45Q03K]
* Brésil-Lula et Flavio Bolsonaro clôturent leurs campagnes avant le premier tour des élections [USN:L6N45P07U]
* AVANT-PAPIER-Brésil-Lula et Bolsonaro au coude-à-coude pour la présidence [USN:L6N45N0MU]
* PORTRAIT-Brésil-Flavio Bolsonaro, la présidentielle en héritage [USN:L6N45L0NC]
* PORTRAIT-Lula porte les espoirs de la gauche, au-delà du Brésil [USN:L8N45L137]
* ENCADRÉ-Brésil-Dans la course à la présidence, les écueils budgétaires sont passés sous silence [USN:L6N45L0SH]

items.title: フーシ派、リヤドのアラムコ施設攻撃と発表　サウジの攻撃に報復
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は３日、サウジアラビアの首都リヤドにあるサウジアラムコの施設を弾道ミサイルと無人機で攻撃したと発表した。イエメンの首都サヌアやその他の州へのサウジの攻撃に対する報復だとしている。

これに先立ち、リヤドにあるアラムコ施設の近くから大量の煙と炎が上がったとの目撃者情報が出ていた。

アラムコ施設への攻撃について、サウジ当局は今のところ確認していない。アラムコもコメント要請に応じていない。

サウジとフーシ派の衝突は激しさを増し、フーシ派はサウジの都市やエネルギーインフラへの攻撃を強めている。

フーシ派は先週、サウジ西部ヤンブーにあるアラムコの施設をミサイルと無人機で攻撃したと発表した。サウジはその際、フーシ派がタイフとヤンブー周辺に向けて撃った弾道ミサイル６発を撃墜したと説明したが、アラムコ施設の被害については明らかにしなかった。

items.title: OpenAI safety employee quits, says 'time for trial and error is over'
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: AI companies are not being "nearly careful enough," David Robinson wrote in the Atlantic.
items.body:
A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the company's approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures.
Writing in "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken," published by the Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems.
"The time for trial and error is over," Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation.
Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls "iterative deployment," releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge.
The comments add to a [USN:L6N45L0PN TEXT:"debate within the AI industry"] over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. [USN:L4N45L05X TEXT:"OpenAI"] and rival [USN:L6N45L00I TEXT:"Anthropic"] have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed, or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly.
Robinson, who said he spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches, wrote: "As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."
"We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

items.title: Trump shares Republican senator's phone number in feud over time switch
items.author: Bo Erickson
items.creator: Bo Erickson
items.summary: Less afternoon sunlight makes it harder to play more than 14 holes of golf, Trump said.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump shared online the supposed phone number of a Republican US senator on Saturday in an escalating dispute over making daylight saving time permanent.
In a social media post, the president urged people to call a phone number he said belonged to Senator Tom Cotton, an Arkansas Republican who opposes the Trump-backed Sunshine Protection Act. The act would end the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour.
Trump says most Americans want more afternoon sunlight, but Cotton has argued the change would plunge early risers into darkness in winter.
"Everybody in Arkansas, Tom Cotton, a friend of mine, is holding up a very important Bill," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
Cotton did not directly respond to Trump's statement, but posted on X:
"No one likes changing the clock, me included, but Congress has enacted permanent Daylight Savings Time multiple times before and repealed it each time once Americans experienced absurdly late sunrises in the winter.
"Arkansans don't want their kids going to school in the pitch dark, and I'll always put Arkansas first."
When Reuters called the number Trump gave for Cotton, it went directly to a voicemail box that did not identify itself as belonging to the senator.
Supporters of permanent daylight saving time say adjusting clocks disrupts sleep and increases road accidents, while critics argue later winter sunrises would leave children traveling to school and commuters heading to work in the dark.
GOLFING ARGUMENT Trump on Saturday published three Truth Social posts — one in the morning and two in the afternoon — focused on daylight saving time. In a subsequent five-minute session with journalists at the White House, he spent more than half the time talking about the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour .
Most US states have observed the time switch since the 1960s. Clocks this year are slated to switch back to standard time on November 1.
"It discombobulates everybody," Trump said, complaining to reporters that losing afternoon daylight caused lateness for meetings and dinner and made it difficult to play more than 14 holes of golf. He also suggested that more daylight would reduce crime.
"You know who wants it? The farmers want it. You know who wants it? Sports want it," Trump told reporters before heading to a [USN:L1N45O0PX TEXT:"campaign rally in Ohio"] .
"Professional sports and amateurs that would like to play tennis at night, would like to play golf a little bit without having to run home after 14 holes."
Trump, an avid golfer, earlier shared an October 1 letter from PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, writing: "The PGA TOUR, as an example, needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments."
POLITICAL CONSIDERATIONS After Cotton published his statement, the president responded with a post that framed the matter in political terms.
"Give the Republican Party a Senatorial WIN, for a change! … TAKE THE WIN TOM, JUST TAKE THE WIN! YOU NEED IT, AND SO DOES OUR BELOVED REPUBLICAN PARTY!" Trump wrote.
Cotton is running for reelection but his race is not considered competitive, as Trump received more than 64% of the Arkansas vote in the 2024 presidential election.
The US House of Representatives passed the bill in July, but Cotton is not alone in the Senate. Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, this week called the bill "[USN:L1N45O0H3 TEXT:"dead as disco"]" and said he did not think that Senate Majority Leader John Thune would bring the measure for a vote.
The offices of Cotton and Thune did not respond to requests for comment.
Saturday's post targeting Cotton is not the first time Trump has shared a senator's phone number to make a point. During his first presidential campaign in 2015, Trump [USN:KCN0PV26U TEXT:"read"] Senator Lindsey Graham's phone number at a rally and dismissed the South Carolina Republican as an "idiot."
They later reconciled, with the [USN:L6N43E02O TEXT:"late Graham"] becoming one of Trump's highest-profile allies in Congress.

LONDON: Two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court on Saturday (Oct 3) charged with plotting acts of terrorism involving the use of a homemade bomb to attack the Jewish community in northern England at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran.
Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were arrested on Sep 20 at the start of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, when they are accused of carrying out "hostile" surveillance on potential Jewish targets in Manchester, prosecutors say.
These targets included the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park synagogue, the scene of a deadly attack almost a year ago in which two Jewish worshippers were killed, prosecutor Mark Luckett told Westminster Magistrates' Court.
ALLEGED PLOT INVOLVED HOMEMADE DEVICE "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device," Luckett said.

He said the men were accused of being in contact with a third party who is alleged to have directed and coordinated the attack planning and provided instructions on how to assemble a homemade device, which prosecutors allege would have been made from chlorine and brake fluid.
"It's assessed that this individual is also an Iranian national and most likely operating from within Iran," Luckett said.

The court was told both men had come to Britain from Europe in small boats. Salehi had arrived in 2020 and had been granted asylum, while Ahmadyan came in 2023 and his asylum claim was still outstanding, Luckett said.
The men did not enter a plea and were remanded in custody until their next hearing at London's Old Bailey court on Oct 23.
The case comes a week after Britain said Iran was believed to be involved in a suspected plot to target the RAF Fairford air base which the US military has used to carry out raids against targets in Iran, leading to a dual British-Iranian national being arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts.
Police said on Saturday he had been released on police bail while the investigation continues. British counterterrorism police have said the Manchester allegations were not connected in any way to the Fairford investigation.
Iran has rejected accusations of involvement in a number of plots in Britain in recent years, and said allegations it was connected to the Fairford incident were baseless.
Britain has also seen a significant rise in antisemitism since the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023 that triggered the subsequent war in Gaza, including a series of attacks on Jewish sites in London earlier this year.
"It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime," Home Secretary (interior minister) Shabana Mahmood said in a statement.
"They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement."

items.title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Aramco facility in Riyadh with missiles, drones
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
items.body:
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Saturday they had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen's Sanaa and other provinces.
A large plume of smoke and fire was seen rising in the vicinity of an Aramco facility in Riyadh earlier on Saturday, a witness told Reuters.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of an attack on an Aramco facility. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The reported attack comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure.
The Houthis said last week they had attacked Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu with missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia said at the time that it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards Taif and the Yanbu area, but did not report damage to Aramco facilities.

items.title: In crude Ohio rally speech, Trump says he may not help if Democrats win
items.author: Bo Erickson, Nandita Bose
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Nandita Bose
items.summary: "Just get out and vote," Trump said at a rally for Republican candidates. "If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big, and we're going to shove it up their ass."
items.body:
US President Donald Trump used an Ohio rally on Saturday to mix profane attacks on Democrats with promises of financial help if Republicans win the midterms and a warning that he would be less willing to work with the state if Democrats prevail.
"Just get out and vote," Trump said at a rally for Republican candidates, including US Senator Jon Husted and Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. "If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big, and we're going to shove it up their ass."
Multiple incumbent Republican senators across the country face tough political headwinds in the November 3 elections, with Trump's [USN:L6N45D0XN TEXT:"popularity falling"] in recent months as higher prices persist for gasoline and other staples amid the US-Israeli war with Iran. Both Husted and Ramaswamy are in competitive races against Democratic opponents.
Former US Senator Sherrod Brown is running against Husted. Amy Acton is facing Ramaswamy.
OHIO A KEY STATE IN MIDTERMS Polls have suggested that Democrats could gain ground in the midterms, which will decide control of the narrowly divided House of Representatives and Senate, but Trump said Republicans would do better than critics expect. "I think we're going to have a big surprise because they don't know what's happening," he told the crowd in Vandalia, Ohio.
Ohio's is among eight US Senate races rated competitive. The state has turned into a campaign battlefield over [USN:L6N45916H TEXT:"data centers"] and culture war issues such as youth transgender surgeries.
Trump repeatedly attacked Democrats during his speech, at one point calling them "dumb son of a bitches," while arguing that maintaining Republican control would give Ohio officials a direct line to his administration and make it easier for the state to secure federal help.
He said Ohio's elected Republican officials frequently call him seeking money for the state, adding that he would be less inclined to accommodate Democrats if they win key races. Referring to Acton, Trump said: "But I'm not going to help her."
Husted is counting on Trump to motivate supporters who might otherwise skip the midterms, but the senator also directly criticized Brown, a veteran Democrat, as someone who has accomplished little in his political career. "He's been in office for 50 years — can you name one thing that he has done for you?" Husted said at the rally.
A spokesperson for Brown's campaign criticized Husted for backing Trump's policy on Iran and said Husted supported "sweetheart tax deals" that lured data centers to Ohio.
"Jon Husted puts corporations and billionaires first every time, and we all pay for it," Brown spokesperson Lauren Chou said in an email to Reuters.
Trump garnered more than 55% of the Ohio vote in the 2024 presidential election, but economic concerns since then have sunk his approval ratings.
Ohio gasoline prices increased 35% over the past year to $4.16 per gallon on average, according to AAA, which compiles data on automobile travel. Trump's trade policy with Canada has led to retaliatory Canadian tariffs that affect about $3 billion worth of Ohio exports, based on 2025 figures, according to a CBC report.
DEBATE ON DATA CENTERS Talking to reporters shortly before addressing Saturday's rally, Husted said the US has to win the Iran war "on our terms" and in the interim, he is "showing people that I'm fighting for lower prices."
He spoke to a sympathetic crowd at the rally, but he also needs to sell his message to people like independent voter Jonathan Smith.
Smith, a 19-year-old construction worker, held a sign reading, "Where are my lower gas prices?" outside his former high school in Vandalia, north of Dayton.
"I've got a wedding to save up for, and with gas prices continuously going up, it's getting harder and harder to put aside money," said Smith, adding he is still deciding whom to vote for in the Senate race.
Outside political groups have poured [USN:L6N458188 TEXT:"tens of millions"] of dollars into Ohio, making Husted-Brown the second-most-expensive Senate race in the country, according to Federal Election Commission filings.
Rallygoers shared mixed opinions on the hot-button issue of data centers in the state.
"I'm not huge on the AI data centers," Samuel Clevenger, 20, said when discussing Husted's candidacy. But the apprentice plumber said he was encouraged to vote by Trump's attention to the state, as well as his 2025 policy capping taxes on overtime.
On the other side of the rally venue, Brenda White, 60, held a sign encouraging building in her northeastern Ohio town: "DATA CENTER SOUTH LORAIN."
As Husted met voters in the bleachers, she urged the senator to support the center's construction in place of a steel mill. "You want a data center there?" Husted asked.
Before White posed for her photo with Husted, a man in the senator's entourage asked: "Can we do it without the sign?"

items.title: New term gives US Supreme Court's Thomas and Alito more chances to wield power
items.author: Jan Wolfe
items.creator: Jan Wolfe
items.summary: The two oldest and most conservative justices are at the height of their influence.
items.body:
The new US Supreme Court term that begins on Monday presents opportunities for its two eldest and most conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, to help push US law further rightward on contentious issues such as gun rights, religion in public schools and voting restrictions.
Thomas, 78, has served on the top US judicial body since 1991, making him the [USN:L1N41E02Q TEXT:"second-longest-serving justice"] in American history. Alito, 76, has served since 2006.
Earlier in their tenures, they often found themselves in dissent in major decisions, but the court, with a 6-3 conservative majority since 2020, has shifted dramatically to the right. Thomas and Alito now are perhaps at the height of their influence and have been lavished with praise by Republican President Donald Trump .
'WHY LEAVE?' If either were to retire, that would clear the way for Trump to nominate a younger conservative replacement who could serve for decades in the lifetime position. But, at least for now, according to legal experts, they appear more interested in wielding that power than stepping aside.
"They have been waiting for a long time to be in the position," political science professor Kevin McMahon of Trinity College in Connecticut said of Thomas and Alito. "So why leave?"
During the court's term that ended in June, Thomas and Alito helped deliver long-sought victories to the conservative legal movement. These included a [USN:S0N3YR013 TEXT:"ruling"] expanding presidential control over regulatory agencies, and a [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"decision"] further limiting the scope of the Voting Rights Act, the landmark 1965 law intended to eliminate racial discrimination in voting.
Thomas and Alito have been Trump's most reliable votes in cases involving his extraordinary exertion of presidential powers. [USN:L1N45H0WL TEXT:"More such cases are coming"] during the new nine-month term, including two involving Trump's hardline [USN:S0N43101E TEXT:"immigration policies"].
The court's docket also includes November 3 arguments in a [USN:L1N4130K0 TEXT:"challenge"] to a Colorado law requiring preschools receiving taxpayer money to enroll children of same-sex couples, the latest clash between religious rights and LGBT protections to reach the justices.
The justices also may take up a case examining whether a Texas law that requires public elementary and high schools to display the [USN:L1N45G0IM TEXT:"biblical Ten Commandments"] in classrooms comports with the US Constitution's prohibition on the government establishing or endorsing any particular religion or promoting religion over nonreligion.
On December 2, the court will [USN:S0N3YR01V TEXT:"hear"] arguments over whether states can ban AR-15s and other semiautomatic rifles, an opportunity for the conservative justices to further expand gun rights. Thomas and Alito have been instrumental in major guns rulings since 2008.
On December 8, the court will [USN:S0N41Y01G TEXT:"consider"] whether Arizona can mandate that people registering to vote provide proof of citizenship, a Republican-backed measure critics have called an effort to make it harder for groups who tend to support Democratic candidates to register.
Legal experts said these cases give Thomas and Alito chances to build on some of their most influential earlier rulings and target more Supreme Court precedents they consider misguided.
"They have more they want to accomplish, and I expect them to keep pushing on a host of issues," McMahon said, adding that they even may envision themselves serving as a check on a potential future Democratic president beginning in 2029.
"They're still in their seventies," McMahon said. "And for a Supreme Court justice, it's not unprecedented that you stay on the bench well into your eighties."
'LEGENDS, BOTH' Thomas and Alito backed every major Trump administration policy that came before the court last term, unlike the three conservative justices Trump appointed during his first term — Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett. Those three all have compiled very conservative records as justices but in a few major cases sided against Trump.
Trump [USN:L6N45N0QS TEXT:"told"] Time magazine this week he regretted nominating all three, calling them disloyal.
"I gave them the position of a lifetime, and they vote against me often," Trump said.
Thomas and Alito, on the other hand, are "[USN:FWN4570D3 TEXT:"legends, both"]," Trump said last month after they dissented from a decision that blocked his plans to restrict mail-in voting.
"Alito and Thomas are the two who have figured out how to never get into Trump's doghouse," University of Minnesota political science professor Timothy Johnson said.
Alito rejected the notion that he is a rubber stamp for Trump and his administration, telling the Wall Street Journal in August: "I vote in every case the way I think the case should be decided. If that means a high correlation with what Trump wants, fine. If it means zero correlation with what Trump wants, fine as well."
'A VALUABLE CONTRIBUTION' Speculation among court watchers about a possible vacancy has ramped up as the two men draw closer to the average age of retirement for Supreme Court justices since 2000 — about 80 years old — and with the November 3 US congressional elections looming.
If Democrats take control of the Senate, they could try to block Trump's nominee to fill any vacancy created by the retirement or death of a sitting justice.
Alito tamped down retirement speculation for now, telling the Wall Street Journal: "Obviously, I'm here for another term."
The term runs through the end of June.
In a CBS News interview excerpt released on Friday, Alito said he thought about retiring this year, calling retirement something someone his age must think about every year.
"But I thought that I could still make a valuable contribution, which is why I became a justice and a judge in the first place," Alito said.
"It's too hard to predict, for anybody, particularly when you reach a certain age, what your situation will be a year from now, two years from now, and so forth," Alito said. "And it's too hard to predict what the political situation will be, and what any president might do with respect to a replacement."
ABORTION RIGHTS Alito has a lot of influence in conversations among the court's conservatives, said Peter Canellos, author of a recent Alito biography titled "Revenge for the Sixties."
"A lot of the action on the Supreme Court right now is conservative on conservative," Canellos said. "It's entirely a discussion among conservatives."
Canellos said Alito's influence was highlighted by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, perhaps the most important ruling he has authored. It overturned the 1973 Roe v. Wade precedent that had recognized a woman's constitutional right to have an abortion.
Chief Justice John Roberts, a stalwart conservative, dissented from the portion of Alito's ruling that reversed Roe.
"I think over the years Alito has thought of himself as an instrumental justice," Canellos said. "You can see in many cases, Dobbs included, that his key ability is to bring the three Trump appointees to his side, rather than Chief Justice Roberts' side, when the two of them disagree."
In Dobbs, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh and Barrett joined Alito.
"I suspect that Alito felt that even if he were replaced by a true conservative, which was the core of the argument why he should resign, it was not in any way preordained that that person would have the kind of influence that he has," Canellos added.
Alito has long criticized a 1990 Supreme Court precedent that limits the ability of people to seek religious exemptions from generally applicable laws. Religious rights advocates have said that ruling infringes on First Amendment protections for free exercise of religion. The 1990 ruling specifically held that the First Amendment does not protect people who participate in illegal acts — in that case, the use of an illegal hallucinogenic drug — as part of a religious ceremony.
The religious freedom case being argued in November, called St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, gives Alito and the other conservative justices a chance to cast doubt on the 1990 precedent, known as Employment Division v. Smith.
'WHY NOT CONTINUE?' The case involving state-level bans on assault-style rifles may give Thomas a chance to clarify a test he laid out in one of his most impactful rulings, a 2022 case called New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen.
Under this test, gun control measures must be "consistent with this nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation" — not simply advance an important government interest — in order to comply with the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms. Some judges have said this wording does not provide clear guidance, producing inconsistent results.
"He has clearly expressed frustration that his colleagues have dodged reviews of assault-weapon prohibitions, making these consolidated challenges from Connecticut and Illinois a long-sought vehicle to establish a nationwide constitutional rule that includes these specific guns," Johnson said of Thomas.
Thomas has not addressed retirement rumors, but in the past has hinted at a lengthy tenure.
McMahon said Thomas may want to become the longest-serving justice, a milestone he would reach in May 2028.
"If you're that close, and you have the setup that he has, why not continue?" McMahon asked.
items.raw_description: The two oldest and most conservative justices are at the height of their influence.

WASHINGTON, Oct 3 : US President Donald Trump spent Tuesday showcasing his administration’s approach to AI — touting the US government’s new AI chatbot, dining with tech titans at the White House, and announcing a voluntary agreement with those executives that he said would address growing fears about the technology's safety.
The display signaled that Trump is eager to show he is addressing growing voter concerns about AI's dangers without imposing restrictions that could hamper the technology's development, AI safety advocates said. The safety agreement with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Trump described it as “morally binding.”
“This was an attempt to give the impression that the government is listening to these concerns without undercutting what has been a very clear and consistent line from this administration: that regulation and governance inherently impede innovation,” said Kat Duffy, who runs an AI team at the nonpartisan Council on Foreign Relations.
Whether voters buy Trump's effort in the run-up to US midterm elections on November 3 remains to be seen. Public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months. Three-quarters of Americans worry that AI companies have not gone far enough to prevent AI from causing serious harm to society, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published September 22. A series of security events has also underscored how advanced AI can act unpredictably.

Hundreds of OpenAI AI agents broke out of their testing environment in July and attacked the infrastructure of AI platform Hugging Face. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, saying that the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade." His words, and others, sparked a flurry of calls from US lawmakers for AI regulation. 
Through it all, Trump has largely dismissed those concerns, saying that government restrictions would make it harder for American companies to compete against their Chinese counterparts. He has repeatedly said that US law enforcement agencies such as the Justice Department serve as sufficient guardrails, and that no new rules are needed. He also directed his administration to call AI "super intelligence," part of an effort to improve the reputation of an unpopular technology. 
The concerns have become prominent enough to make their way into late-night comedy. In late September, "Saturday Night Live" satirized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, one of the industry's most outspoken voices on AI risks — even as his company readies a public stock sale that could value it at $2 trillion — with cast member Jane Wickline portraying the executive.
"AI is not a weapon, it’s a tool: A tool for building weapons. And I urge you to urge me to stop," Wickline said as Amodei.
CONCERNS ABOUT ENFORCEMENT
The accord, inked Tuesday, does include measures that AI safety advocates have sought, including calling for “robust internal controls” to prevent unauthorized hacks as well as partnering with “independent external auditors.” Those concepts have been included in draft state and federal legislation, and California in September enacted the first state law setting rules for how independent auditors evaluate AI products.
But the one-page White House document did not address details or enforcement mechanisms.
A White House official said in a statement that the agreement will "advance American innovation and strengthen responsible development" of AI models. Trump is expected to name his Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as his top AI adviser, Reuters previously reported, a position he has dubbed "AI czar," even as Clayton stays in his role leading the nation's intelligence agencies.
Representative Ro Khanna, a Democrat representing Silicon Valley, welcomed the idea of "independent auditors" but said that they should report to an independent federal agency.
"They can’t just be auditors that report to (OpenAI CEO) Sam Altman or Dario Amodei," he said. "My concern is the president basically trusting these guys who have a huge profit motive and won’t have the judgment to keep us safe."
Venture capitalist David Sacks, who advises Trump on AI and has been an advocate for unrestricted AI development, said on the social media platform X that securities law and other legal authorities would penalize companies that fail to address problems uncovered by internal controls or auditors.
But AI safety advocates told Reuters those authorities can only address harms after they occur, saying the threats require safeguards designed to prevent large-scale harm before it happens.
Nevertheless, some AI observers saw the simple fact of hosting the event as an indication that Trump is absorbing the worries.
Trump’s agreement with the tech executives is “a shift toward acknowledging that there are serious safety and security concerns that merit closer coordination between the companies,” said Samuel Hammond, AI policy director at the conservative Foundation for American Innovation.

Source: Reuters

MANILA: The Philippines, chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), expressed concern over an airstrike in Myanmar's Rakhine state that caused deaths, injuries and destruction, and stood ready to facilitate discussions within the regional bloc on how best to assist Myanmar.
"The Philippines is closely monitoring developments and expresses concern over the attacks which resulted in destruction, loss of lives and injuries to those affected," Foreign Affairs Assistant Secretary for ASEAN Affairs Ana Marie Hernando said in an email response on Saturday (Oct 3).
As ASEAN chair, Manila said it remained mindful of the views of all member states and would continue to be guided by the regional bloc's consensus-based approach.
The Philippines said it stood ready to facilitate discussions within ASEAN on ways to assist Myanmar, in line with the common aspiration of finding a solution that is "Myanmar-owned and led".
Monday's Kyauktaw airstrike, Rakhine's deadliest such attack since a December hospital bombing, killed 50 people and wounded dozens more.
Myanmar has been locked in a nationwide civil war since a 2021 coup, with an alliance of armed groups, including the Arakan Army, fighting against the military.
The protracted conflict has since killed around 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million in the impoverished Southeast Asian nation.

items.title: High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement
items.author: CNA
items.summary: While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade.

High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement

While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade.

Police officers stand in front of protestors amid tear gas as protesting students carry out blockading action near the Kerichen high school in Brest, western France, on Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Fred Tanneau)

AUBERVILLIERS: Maisa, a 17-year-old in a poor Paris suburb who aspires to be an English teacher, joined tens of thousands of other students and their supporters this week in protests that spread across France over dilapidated schools, classroom overcrowding and teacher shortages. 
At Lycee Le Corbusier school in Aubervilliers, a suburb north of Paris in the Seine-Saint-Denis department, protesters said schools in poor neighbourhoods like theirs faced the worst conditions.
“Last year I took the high school French exam without a French teacher, and teachers have a huge impact,” Maisa said.
"These are not conditions to study in."

As protests raged at more than 1,200 French high schools this week, police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets in some cases. More than 5,000 people were arrested, and some protesters were seriously hurt with eye injuries, broken teeth and blows to the head. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it a "climate of unacceptable violence" and called for order.
Amelia, 15, joined Maisa in the crowd outside the school gates and held a sign reading, "Our address should not decide our future". She said she was demonstrating to demand the same rights as students elsewhere in the country.      
"The education authority is not investing enough in the suburbs. It's classist and racist," she said. 
Ulysse Rabate, a political scientist at Paris 8 University, said the protests show the way that France's marginalised urban neighbourhoods are increasingly influencing national politics.
"When there is a collapse of the public service, of public education, those who feel it the most, and the most violently, are those at bottom," he said.

A French firefighter extinguishes a fire on the street amid clashes between protesters and police during a high school students protest in Pantin near Paris as part of nationwide protests to demand the hiring of substitute teachers, increased resources and better learning conditions, as more than 400 schools remain closed following days of student protests that have escalated into violence in some places, France, Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Tom Nicholson)

POLITICAL FLASHPOINT The nationwide demonstrations and blockades , which began last week, have become a political flashpoint at a sensitive moment for the government, which announced a series of deeply unpopular spending cuts in its 2027 budget on Thursday.
The education budget is set to increase by a below-inflation 1.7 per cent to €65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions.
The education ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said that education remained a priority and the below-inflation budget increase was due to population decline.
The protests started in the Parisian suburbs, where poverty levels are high, then spread to Paris itself and other French towns, including Marseille, Strasbourg, Tours and Lille. 
At Lycee Le Corbusier, classes including maths, humanities, English and sport have been canceled since the start of the academic year due to a teacher shortage, according to Karima Kara Ali, an elected parent representative. 
In Seine-Saint-Denis, two-thirds of high schools took part in protests on Thursday, the CGT labour union said. Youth, teachers and parents in four towns complained of unsanitary school conditions and chronic staff shortages including of nurses and social workers. 
Louise Paternoster, a representative for the Seine-Saint-Denis branch of the CGT's education union, said the area does not get adequate resources for its student population and their educational needs.
Two-thirds of schools in the department have unfilled teacher positions, according to a union survey.

A student carries a barrier in front of a banner which reads "equal opportunities" suspended on the front of Louis-le-Grand high school in central Paris, on Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Simon Wohlfahrt)

NOT ENOUGH TEACHERS "Our students are losing out on study time. Some schools don't have drinking water. We are not equal to other departments," she said, blaming shortages on government cuts of 3,256 teacher positions nationwide in 2026.
In Pantin, a town on the northeastern edge of Paris, teacher Dilan Roche joined her students as they protested outside their school this week to support their demands and protect them from the police.
"What they wrote on banners, we wrote in a letter to the local education authority: overcrowded classes, no nurses, no social workers - which is problematic for students with learning difficulties, many living in precarity," she said.
While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade, standing at €11,660 in 2024 and €11,910 in 2010, according to education ministry data. 
The last nationwide high school protest movement on this scale demanding more funding came in the 1990s. That followed the government sharply expanding access to the baccalauréat, the school-leaving exam that typically paves the way to university, without providing schools with sufficient additional resources, said Professor Clemence Cardon-Quint at Paul Valery University, who researches education funding. 
The movement won an increase in funding, but spending per student later stagnated despite growing demands on schools.
Cardon-Quint said students and teachers have taken on additional responsibilities over the years, including navigating Parcoursup, the university admissions system introduced in 2018 and criticised by some students and teachers as opaque and discriminatory.
"In a period of budgetary restraint, it is more difficult to reduce inequalities," said Cardon-Quint.

Source: Reuters/ec

items.body:
［ドバイ／エルサレム　３日　ロイター］ - アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のドバイからイスラエルのテルアビブに向かっていたＵＡＥの格安航空（ＬＣＣ）フライドバイ機内で副操縦士が機長を刺した事件で、ＵＡＥの検事総長は３日、副操縦士が飛行中に「テロ」攻撃を実行しようとしたと述べた。国営通信ＷＡＭが伝えた。  　

ハマド・サイフ・アル・シャムシ検事総長は「フライドバイＦＺ１０７３便を巡る事件の捜査で、副操縦士がテロ攻撃を企てていたことが判明した」と述べた。 

副操縦士は操縦室内に備え付けられている非常時用のおの（クラッシュアックス） で機長を襲い、機長に代わって操縦しようとしたという。検事総長は、容疑者の動機を含めＦＺ１０７３便を巡る捜査は続いており、「必要な手続き」が済み次第、結果を公表すると述べた。 

ＵＡＥ大統領の上級顧問を務めるアンワル・ガルガシュ氏は、ＵＡＥはテロを一切容認せず、過激主義的な言説にも寛容な姿勢は取らないとＸに投稿した。 

ＵＡＥ当局は副操縦士の身元を公表していないが、関係者は、オマーン国籍のハマム・アルハマミ容疑者だと述べた。捜査について説明を受けた別の関係筋も、その名前を確認した。ＵＡＥ当局は、容疑者の身元に関するロイターの問い合わせに返答していない。

フライドバイの広報担当者は、事件の詳しい状況は引き続き調査中で、これ以上のコメントはできないと述べた。

＜イスラエル、捜査に参加の意向、オマーンは沈黙＞ 

副操縦士は、同機が緊急着陸したサウジアラビアで身柄を拘束された。サウジ内務省によると、機長とともに１日朝にサウジからアブダビに向かった。

同機の搭乗客は大半がイスラエル人だった。イスラエル政府当局者は２日、ＵＡＥ主導の捜査に加わり、何が起きたのかを解明し、容疑者の動機や経歴を調べるとロイターに語った。捜査について説明を受けた関係筋は２日、イスラエルの当局者がＵＡＥで副操縦士を事情聴取する見通しだと述べた。どの機関や当局が聴取するかは明らかにしなかった。

副操縦士について、イスラエル側は早い段階からオマーン国籍だと指摘していた。イスラエルとオマーンの間に正式な外交関係はなく、イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相は、そうした国の操縦士がイスラエル便を運航することは認められていないと述べている。副操縦士がテルアビブ便の乗務に就いた経緯は分かっていない。オマーンは事件についてコメントしていない。

items.title: 独経済、今年1％前後成長も　財政支出と輸出寄与と連銀総裁
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［フランクフルト　２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［フランクフルト　２日　ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後になる可能性があると述べた。堅調な輸出需要と政府投資が寄与する。同中銀が６月に示した予測（０．５％）の２倍となる。

ドイツは過去３年間ほとんど成長していない。イラン戦争に起因するエネルギー価格高騰が産業に打撃を与えている。

ナーゲル氏は講演で、生産は予想外に底堅いと指摘した。潜在成長率は依然として低いものの、ドイツは景気循環上の回復局面にあるとの認識を示した。

「年平均で１％前後の実質経済成長となる可能性は十分にある」と述べ、「３年間の停滞を経て、これは確かに小さいながらも歓迎すべき兆しとなるだろう」とした。

ナーゲル氏は、連邦政府の国防やインフラなどに重点を置いた財政支出を成長けん引役の一つとし、予想外に堅調な海外需要の恩恵も受けているとした。

ドイツの主要経済研究所も先月下旬に、今年と来年の経済成長率予測を上方修正した。今年の成長率予測は０．６％から１．３％に引き上げられた。

items.title: トランプ氏、公的医療保険加入者に90ドル給付表明　2000万人超
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kanishka Singh

［ワシントン　２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Kanishka Singh

［ワシントン　２日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は、高齢者向け公的医療保険「メディケア」に加入する米国民２０００万人超に対し、毎月の保険料負担を軽減するため、１人当たり９０ドルを一時金として支給すると表明した。

トランプ氏は２日深夜、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）への投稿で、給付金は「メディケア改善基金」から拠出すると説明。同基金には、メディケアの出来高払い制度の改善を目的として議会から２０億ドルが拠出されているとした。

ホワイトハウスのウェブサイトによると、対象の高齢者の大半に１０月上旬に９０ドルが銀行口座に直接振り込まれる。口座振り込みを利用していない対象者には、メディケアに登録した住所に小切手を送付する。発送も１０月上旬になるという。

トランプ氏は１１月の中間選挙を前に、有権者にばらまき的施策を打ち出している。９月には、中間選挙で勝利すれば成人に５０００ドルの「トランプ配当」を給付すると提案した。

政権は、１００万人近い米国民への５００ドルの給付も進めている。ホワイトハウスは、この５００ドルの給付について、医療保険制度改革法（ＡＣＡ）に基づく保険の加入者から過剰に徴収されたとする保険料の払い戻しだと説明している。給付は全米を対象としたものでなく、連邦政府の医療保険加入サイトを利用する３０州の一部住民に限られる。対象州には主要な激戦州が多く含まれ、選挙戦略の専門家らは、一部の選挙戦の結果に影響を及ぼす可能性があると指摘している。

items.title: ゴルフ＝畑岡と山下が7位、首位と3打差　ロッテ選手権
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［２日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのロッテ選手権は２日、米ハワイ州エワビーチのホアカレイＣＣ（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、前日３６位の畑岡奈紗が７バーディー、ノーボギーの６５をマークし、通算９アンダーの１３５で７位に浮上した。

１０位で出た山下美夢有も８バーディー、３ボギーの６７で回り、通算９アンダーで畑岡と並ぶ７位。首位とは３打差につけた。

岩井明愛は６９で回り、通算７アンダーの１３７で１４位。西郷真央は７０で通算６アンダーの１３８とし、２２位に後退した。

岩井千怜、竹田麗央、笹生優花は３３位。吉田優利は４５位、櫻井心那と西村優菜は５７位で、そのほかの日本選手は予選落ちとなった。

上位では、ポリー・マック（ドイツ）とジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）がともに６５をマークし、通算１２アンダーの１３２で首位。１打差の１１アンダーにカロリナ・メルグラティ（イタリア）とユン・イナ（韓国）が続いた。

items.title: Analysis:AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out
items.author: CNA

Analysis:AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out

FILE PHOTO: "AI Artificial Intelligence" words, a keyboard and a robotics hand in this illustration taken, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

(Updated: 03 Oct 2026 03:15PM)

FAST

LONDON, Oct 3 : Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital.
Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC, almost matching the value of outstanding US Treasuries. It "dwarfs" what was spent in the railroad or dotcom booms, even after adjusting for inflation, PwC said.
Meanwhile, Anthropic, just one of the major firms in the AI race, plans to spend $518 billion in coming years, according to the IPO prospectus seen by Reuters, which is more than 100 times its 2025 revenue. Its backers say AI technology will be more transformational than the advent of steam engines and the industrialization they powered.
Yet lurking behind the dizzying projections and huge outlays by AI companies, alongside sky-high valuations, lie assumptions about vast broad-based productivity gains and future profits with little evidence so far - or historical precedent - to be sure they can deliver, economists say.

PRODUCTIVITY GAINS 'REMAIN ELUSIVE'
JP Morgan wrote in August that broad-based productivity gains in the US, which leads the AI race, "remain elusive", raising questions about the sustainability of AI valuations.
A Bain & Company study said productivity gains from existing markets would not be enough to justify current outlays and "entirely new markets must emerge to close the funding gap", suggesting those could range from using AI-guided robots to developing new materials for batteries and semiconductors.
US hyperscalers - the companies rolling out infrastructure around the world like Google, Amazon and Microsoft - and others in the AI race needed to find more than $4.2 trillion of new revenue in the next five years to fund the buildout, Bain said.
"The question is whether the applications arrive in time to pay for it," according to the study, published last month.
Few doubt the potential of AI to transform everything from work in an office to research labs, just as past revolutions shrank journey times from days to hours or connected the world at the touch of a keyboard.
What seems more immutable is the maths behind securing a return on investment or the deadlines for repaying loans, leaving economists to work out the implications for the global economy beyond the ups and downs of investment cycles.
"Historical precedent suggests that technology-driven booms often end when infrastructure buildouts cease to deliver sufficient returns," JP Morgan wrote.
Using the example of Nvidia, the US company whose chips are the backbone of the AI revolution, JP Morgan estimated US productivity gains would need to be 3 per cent to 5 per cent annually over the next 10 years to justify its valuation. That would be a substantial increase from the baseline expectation of the US Congressional Budget Office of 1.75 per cent annual productivity growth for that period.
For the US alone - which according to some estimates accounts for about three quarters of the global AI investment total - investment will run as high as about $9 trillion from 2025 to 2032, equivalent to spending 3.2 per cent of US GDP each year, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh.
He estimates the US AI sector would need to generate about $3.55 trillion in annual revenue by 2032 to earn a 10 per cent return on investment. It earns a fraction of that now.
The leveraged structure of much of the debt funding AI infrastructure also means "a relatively modest deterioration in demand, delays, or asset values can therefore produce much larger losses," he wrote in a conference paper, revised in October.
AI AND 'THE RATE OF NEW WONDERS'
The dizzying numbers have not stopped US AI bosses speaking with an otherworldly zeal about changes afoot.
Anthropic's Dario Amodei has said an AI future could be "a thing of transcendent beauty", while OpenAI's Sam Altman has said "the rate of new wonders being achieved will be immense" as models learn to improve themselves and accelerate breakthroughs.
Jasjeet Sekhon, chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind, told a summit at UC Berkeley in August that this self-teaching, known as recursive self-improvement, was a "key part of the investment thesis", and that it could, if achieved, deliver unprecedented productivity gains.
Recursive self-improvement, while potentially delivering exponential AI advances, has also raised concerns about existential risks to humanity.
Yet the pace of change in productivity might still end up lagging the timelines needed by corporate accounts departments.
Diane Coyle, an economist at Britain's Cambridge University, said the productivity impact of past revolutionary technologies had usually taken about 10 to 50 years to feed through.
Anthropic's economics team modeled a range of scenarios for how much extra growth AI would deliver at an annual rate in 2030. Assuming a baseline of 2 per cent in a non-AI environment, it suggested growth of 2.4 per cent in a scenario with modest AI impact, 5.4 per cent in a substantial scenario and 15.4 per cent in an extreme scenario.
Higher growth would mean more jobs lost, it said, without assigning probabilities for any of the outcomes.
Amodei forecast last year that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. For now, however, some researchers say it appears to have been limited to making it harder for those seeking office work to find a job.
Studies in the US and Britain have pointed to a slowdown in early career hiring for white-collar positions performing tasks at which AI is adept, even if overall employment remains strong.
Researchers at Stanford University said in August that employment of workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed industries, such as accountants and paralegals, was 19 per cent lower than for jobs that AI found hard to replicate, like janitors and builders.
Yet even if the promised transformation takes longer than numbers surrounding AI companies imply, real economic benefits should stay - just as trains still ran after the Panic of 1873 that bankrupted railroad barons, while the internet didn't shut down after the 1990s dotcom bubble burst.
"History is our friend in trying to understand this," said Coyle. "As long as one is left with the infrastructure that's needed to support all the productivity effects down the road, that's okay."

items.title: アップル、Ｍａｃのアクセス権限制御強化へ　ＡＩリスク対策
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソフト（ＯＳ）を修正すると明らかにした。人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェントがＭａｃ内の全データへのアクセスを求めた場合に、利用者がより明確に認識し対応できるようにする。

メタ・プラットフォームズのＡＩエージェント「Ｍｕｓｅ」について、一部ユーザーから、機密性の高い個人情報にアクセスされたとの批判が出ている。

アップルのスマートフォン「ｉＰｈｏｎｅ」やタブレット端末「ｉＰａｄ」では、「サンドボックス化」と呼ばれる仕組みにより、初期設定ではどのアプリも別のアプリ内のデータにアクセスできない。一方、Ｍａｃはより柔軟な設計となっており、利用者の許可があれば、クラウドバックアップサービスなどのアプリが端末内の全データにアクセスできる「フルディスクアクセス」という設定がある。

アップルは２日、自社のサイトで、一部の開発者が利用者を危険にさらしかねない形でフルディスクアクセス機能を使っていると指摘し、今後、追加の制御機能を導入すると表明した。

「ＡＩエージェントの能力と自律性が高まるにつれ、これほど広範なアクセスに伴うリスクは大幅に増大する。利用者が自身のデータとプライバシーについて十分な情報に基づいて判断できるよう、アクセスを許可する前にこうしたリスクを明確に理解できるようにすることに取り組む」とした。

items.title: 米政権主要閣僚、イラン戦争やフーシ派巡り大統領山荘で協議　米報道
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［２日　ロイター］ - トランプ米政権の主要閣僚が２日、大統領山荘キャンプデービッドに集まり、イラン戦争、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの紛争への対応を協議した。米ニュースサイトのアクシオスが複数の米当局者の話として伝えた。

アクシオスによると、会合はバンス副大統領が主宰し、ルビオ国務長官、ヘグセス国防長官、ウィットコフ大統領特使、ラトクリフ中央情報局（ＣＩＡ）長官、ケイン統合参謀本部議長らが参加した。トランプ政権はこの会合について公表していないが、当局者の１人は「物事が決定された、あるいは少なくとも掘り下げた議論が行われた」と述べたという。

トランプ氏は２日午後、記者団からイランに対する次の一手について問われ、「それを話せば、大ニュースになるだろう」と述べ、「いずれ分かる。非常にうまく進んでいる。イランは厳しい状況だ」と語った。

中東や欧米当局者はロイターに、サウジがフーシ派に対する攻勢を計画していると述べた。紅海の海上輸送路の確保に向け沿岸部で攻勢をかける案や、複数の戦線で同時攻撃を仕掛ける案などが検討されており、向こう数週間以内に開始する可能性があるという。
